summary: Verify conversation claims and hunt for additional gaps in the order-quantity / processor-rate flow

findings.title: CONFIRMED: startProduction aggregates SO items by style, sets orders.saleOrderId, quantity derived from breakup
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/saleOrder.service.ts:311-442 (fn body); 381-386 (byStyle Map); 388-424 (orderItems build); 391-400 (breakupMap dedupe by colorId|sizeId); 429-441 (orderService.createWithItems call); 432 (saleOrderId: id); backend/src/services/order.service.ts:119-146 + 188
findings.detail: `async startProduction(` opens at saleOrder.service.ts:311 and closes at 442. It groups so.items into `byStyle` (381-386), then per style builds a `breakupMap` keyed `${colorId ?? ''}|${sizeId}` summing quantity (391-400), emits one OrderItemInput per style with `breakup` (413-423), and unitPrice = shared price or qty-weighted average (403-412). It passes `saleOrderId: id` at line 432 into orderService.createWithItems. NUANCE: startProduction itself never computes `totalQuantity`; that happens inside order.service.ts createWithItems at 125-127 (`breakupQty = item.breakup.reduce(...)`, `itemTotalQty = breakupQty > 0 ? breakupQty : item.totalQuantity || 0`) and is summed into orders.totalQuantity at 146/188. orders.saleOrderId is set via `sale_orders: { connect: { id: data.saleOrderId } }` at order.service.ts:188. Other gates present in startProduction that the claim omits: startable-status check (327-334), duplicate-active-order guard (340-347), and its own cost-sheet gate (349-364).
findings.planImpact: Claim is safe to build on. If the plan hooks a quantity/rate re-check into the SO->Order hop, the right insertion point is saleOrder.service.ts:426-441 (after orderItems is built, before createWithItems) or inside order.service.ts createWithItems 109-146 where the true totalQuantity is first known — startProduction never sees a totalQuantity number itself.

findings.title: PARTIAL: order.controller createOrder gate is real but accepts a third legacy purpose and picks the cost sheet non-deterministically
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:103-157; specifically 105-115 (ACTIVE), 119-125 (findFirst), 122 (purpose list), 127-132, 134-139 (isApproved), 141-154 (variance)
findings.detail: CONFIRMED parts: the loop at 103 runs per item; 110 throws STYLE_NOT_ACTIVE unless `style.status === 'ACTIVE'`; 135 throws COSTING_NOT_APPROVED unless `costSheet.isApproved`. QUALIFICATIONS: (a) the purpose filter at line 122 is `['RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION','PRODUCTION','PROCUREMENT_PRODUCTION']` — the legacy third value is accepted, not just the two named in the claim; (b) the query at 119-125 is `findFirst` with `supersededById: null` and NO `orderBy` and NO `isApproved` filter — if a style has more than one non-superseded sheet, Postgres may return an unapproved one and creation is blocked at 135 even though an approved sheet exists; (c) two extra gates exist at 141-154 (varianceStatus REQUIRES_APPROVAL / REJECTED). (d) This gate DIVERGES from the parallel gate in saleOrder.service.ts:349-364, which uses findMany with `OR: [{approvalStatus:'APPROVED'},{isApproved:true}]` and does NOT filter supersededById and does NOT check varianceStatus. So the two entry points into order creation enforce different rules.
findings.planImpact: If the plan adds a rate re-check "at order creation", it must be added in BOTH places (order.controller.ts createOrder ~103-157 and saleOrder.service.ts startProduction ~349-364) or the SO->production path will bypass it. Also, any code the plan writes that resolves "the" cost sheet must add an explicit orderBy (e.g. version desc) rather than copying the existing findFirst.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: IN_PRODUCTION clone block is exactly as described, and orderQuantityPcs is absent from the create payload
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:597-743; 599 (trigger), 635-658 (source query), 677-715 (create), 702-713 (sizeBreakdowns), 693-694 (clone lineage); backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4626 (orderQuantityPcs Int?)
findings.detail: Trigger at 599: `if (status === 'IN_PRODUCTION' && previousStatus !== 'IN_PRODUCTION')`. Source rows at 635-646 require ALL of: `purpose:'COSTING'`, `approvalStatus:'APPROVED'`, `costingApprovalStatus: { in: ['APPROVED','ALTERNATE_APPROVED'] }`, `totalCostPerMeter: { not: null }`, scoped by styleFabric.style_components.styleId. Clone create at 677-715 sets clonedFromOrderId: id (693) and clonedFromCadId: costingCad.id (694), copies sizeBreakdowns (sizeName, sizeId, quantity, cadMeters, cadYards) at 705-711. `orderQuantityPcs` appears nowhere in the data object — schema line 4626 declares it `Int?` with no default, so the clone lands with NULL. Only path that reaches this code is PATCH /api/orders/:id/status -> updateOrderStatus (order.controller.ts:563, 589); no other backend site writes orders.status = IN_PRODUCTION (cutting.controller.ts:350 sets work_orders.status, not orders).
findings.planImpact: Confirms the clone site and the single trigger point. A fix that sets orderQuantityPcs on the clone has exactly one insertion point (order.controller.ts:677-714) and one source for the number (`order.order_items[].totalQuantity` for the matching styleId, already loaded at 568-578).

findings.title: CONFIRMED (and worse): clone copies rates verbatim AND drops processorId, rateCardId, costingStyleId and fabricId
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:696-700 vs backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4577-4586, 4664-4669 (rateCardId), 4626 (orderQuantityPcs); contrast backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:1057-1065
findings.detail: Lines 696-700 copy `greigeCostPerMeter`, `processingPricePerMeter`, `totalCostPerMeter`, `costInputMode` straight off costingCad with no lookupRate call anywhere in the block (verified: `lookupRate` is imported only into fabric-costing.controller.ts:8 and fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:22 / laceCostingCalculation.service.ts — never into order.controller.ts). No later code updates a cloned row's rates or quantity (grep for clonedFromOrderId shows only order.controller.ts:620/693 and read-only consumers cad-embroidery.controller.ts:752/788-789). ADDITIONAL, beyond the claim: the create payload also OMITS `processorId`, `rateCardId`, `costingStyleId`, `fabricId`, `componentName`, `patternPartId`, `shrinkagePercent`, `transportCostPerMeter`, `shrinkageCostPerMeter`, `screenCostPerMeter`, `screenType`, `numberOfColors`, `processingBatchGroupColorId`, `createdById`. So the clone carries a price with no record of which processor or which rate-card slab produced it — `rateCardId` is precisely the column that pins processingType+printingType+slab (schema comment at 4664-4667). It also inherits `approvalStatus` default PENDING (schema 4598) and NULL costingApprovalStatus.
findings.planImpact: The plan's "re-lookup rate at order confirmation" cannot even run on the cloned row as written: lookupRate() requires processorId + greigeId + processingType + quantityMeters, and the clone has processorId NULL. The fix must first copy processorId/rateCardId/shrinkagePercent/fabricId/costingStyleId/componentName from the source row, then re-lookup. Copy the field list from the already-correct quantity-change clone at fabric-costing.controller.ts:1007-1075.

findings.title: PARTIAL: no rate check in order creation/confirmation is true, but a rate-change gate DOES exist at Order BOM creation — and it is structurally blind to slab changes
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:304-338 (blocking gate); backend/src/services/processor-rate-validation.service.ts:203-411, 113-150 (getCurrentProcessorRate), 277-283 and 329-335 (slabId passed through), 63-64 (thresholds)
findings.detail: TRUE half: neither createOrder (order.controller.ts:55-330) nor updateOrderStatus (563-756) nor saleOrder.service.startProduction (311-442) nor order.service.createWithItems/updateStatus contains any rate-card, slab, or quantity-vs-costed-quantity comparison. FALSE half: order-bom.service.ts:306 calls `processorRateValidationService.validateCostSheetRates(costSheetId)` and THROWS BusinessError 'RATES_OUTDATED' at 315-325 when any item moved >=5% (threshold constants at processor-rate-validation.service.ts:63-64). CRITICAL LIMITATION: that check re-looks-up the rate at the SAME slab it was costed on — `getCurrentProcessorRate(..., item.rateCard?.slabId)` at 277-283/329-335, and the lookup filters `slabId: slabId || undefined` (line 131). It only detects a rate card whose price changed over time within one slab. It can never detect "the order quantity fell into a different slab". It also silently skips items with `processingCost === 0` (274) or where no current rate row exists (285).
findings.planImpact: Do not write a new validator from scratch and do not claim "nothing exists". The correct shape is to extend processor-rate-validation.service.ts with a quantity-aware variant that calls processor-rate-v2.service.lookupRate(quantityMeters) instead of getCurrentProcessorRate(slabId), and to reuse the existing BusinessError/RATES_OUTDATED contract (order-bom.service.ts:315-325) so the frontend error handling still works.

findings.title: Rate slabs are keyed on METERS, not pieces — any re-lookup must convert cadAverage x pieces
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/processor-rate-v2.service.ts:877-955 (lookupRate, quantityMeters); 899-911 (half-open slab match); 914-923 (top-slab fallback); frontend/src/pages/FabricCostingPage.tsx:1131-1132 (rowQuantityMeters = row.cadMeters * rowQty); 1182-1188
findings.detail: `lookupRate({processorId, processingType, printingType, greigeId, quantityMeters})` matches `processor_quantity_slabs` with `minQuantity <= q AND maxQuantity > q` (half-open, 899-911), falling back to the highest slab when q exceeds all ranges (914-923), then finds the processor_rate_card for that greige+slab (942-949). The only production caller that drives it from a user quantity is the frontend at FabricCostingPage.tsx:1115-1250, which computes `rowQuantityMeters = row.cadMeters * rowQty` (1132) where rowQty is the manually typed orderQuantityPcs. When a row belongs to a processing batch group it instead sends the COMBINED meters across the newest row per styleFabric+width (1139-1176) and also fetches the individual rate for comparison (1192-1200).
findings.planImpact: A re-check at order confirmation / JWO creation must compute meters, not pieces: `cadAverage (or cadMeters) x order_items.totalQuantity`, and must replicate the batch-group aggregation at FabricCostingPage.tsx:1139-1176 or it will look up a smaller quantity than costing did and report a phantom rate rise. Server-side there is no helper for the batch aggregation — it exists only in the React component.

findings.title: The correct quantity-change clone already exists in fabric-costing.controller and is the template order.controller should have used
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:1007-1075; 1057-1058 (processorId), 1059-1061 (rateCardId), 1064 (orderQuantityPcs), 1068-1072 (approval reset); frontend/src/pages/FabricCostingPage.tsx:1396-1405 (quantityChanged -> cloneFromCadId)
findings.detail: When the user changes the quantity on the Fabric Costing page, the frontend sets `fabricWidthCadId: null, cloneFromCadId: <source>` (FabricCostingPage.tsx:1403-1404) and the backend CLONE MODE branch (fabric-costing.controller.ts:1007-1075) creates a new fabric_width_cad that (a) copies CAD geometry from the source, (b) takes the NEW cost values from the request body (which the frontend just re-looked-up via lookupRate), (c) preserves `processorId` (1057), `rateCardId` (1059-1061, with the explicit comment 'clones must keep the rate card too, or the quantity-change copy loses which processor rate produced its numbers'), `costingStyleId` (1041), `componentName`/`patternPartId`/`shrinkagePercent`/`screenCost*` and `orderQuantityPcs` (1064), and (d) resets BOTH approval flags to null (1068-1072). The order-confirmation clone at order.controller.ts:677-715 does none of (b), (c) and only implicitly (d).
findings.planImpact: Strong argument for making the order-confirmation clone call the same code path rather than hand-rolling a second field list. Note the deliberate approval reset at 1068-1072: if the plan re-prices the cloned row at order confirmation it must decide whether the re-priced row stays PENDING (blocking downstream consumers that require APPROVED) or is auto-approved.

findings.title: Cloned RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION rows are orphaned: invisible to every costingStyleId-, fabricId- and approvalStatus-keyed consumer
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/costing.service.ts:710-715 (costingStyleId filter); backend/src/controllers/cad-planning.controller.ts:3641-3655 (requires approvalStatus APPROVED); backend/src/services/orderProductionStatus.service.ts:530-560 (widthCADs via fabricId); backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:1112, 1185-1192
findings.detail: Because the clone omits costingStyleId, fabricId, processorId and lands with approvalStatus PENDING: (1) costing.service.ts:710 queries `fabric_width_cad where costingStyleId = styleId AND purpose in ['COSTING','RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION']` — clones are excluded, so the style budget still sums the original COSTING rows; (2) cad-planning.controller.ts:3641-3655 looks for the RM CAD variance baseline with `purpose:'RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION', approvalStatus:'APPROVED'` — a PENDING clone can never be the baseline; (3) orderProductionStatus.service.ts:530-560 builds the CAD-width picker from `styleFabric.fabricCAD` and `styleFabric.fabric.widthCADs` (fabricId-keyed) — clones have fabricId NULL so they never appear; (4) order-bom.service.ts:1112 sets `selectedCadId: fabricItem.fabricCADId` from the COST SHEET's fabric item, i.e. the original COSTING CAD, and the legacy JSON fallback at 1185-1190 does `findFirst({ where: { costingStyleId: styleId, processorId: { not: null } } })` with NO orderBy — again excluding clones and picking arbitrarily among originals.
findings.planImpact: The clone currently has essentially no downstream cost effect — the real cost path is cost sheet -> order_bom_items.processingCost -> material_requirements.unitPrice -> JWO. A plan that only fixes the clone's rates would fix a dead record. The rate re-check must be applied to the BOM/requirement chain (order-bom.service.ts:1112-1192 and mrp.service.ts:1720-1770), not just to the cloned CAD row.

findings.title: Clone duplicate-guard is unreliable: findFirst without orderBy and a per-order equality check re-clones on every new order
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:608-628; backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4690 (@@unique includes nullable costingStyleId/componentName)
findings.detail: The guard queries `fabric_width_cad.findFirst({ purpose:'RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION', styleFabric.style_components.styleId })` with no orderBy (608-617) and skips only if THAT one arbitrary row's clonedFromOrderId === this order id (620). Consequences: (a) a second order for the same style always re-clones, accumulating RM rows; (b) with several RM rows present, which row findFirst returns is undefined, so re-entering IN_PRODUCTION for the same order may or may not skip; (c) the table unique key `@@unique([costingStyleId, componentName, styleFabricId, cutableWidth, purpose, approvalStatus])` (schema:4690) cannot stop duplicates because the clone leaves costingStyleId and componentName NULL and Postgres treats NULLs as distinct. Failures are swallowed per item into rawMatResults (728-741) and returned as `rawMaterialCalculation.results` (748-754) rather than raised.
findings.planImpact: If the plan starts writing meaningful rates/quantities onto clones, duplicate accumulation becomes a costing correctness problem, not just clutter. Either scope the guard by `clonedFromOrderId: id` directly in the where clause, or make the clone set costingStyleId+componentName so the existing unique index bites.

findings.title: Clone can hide the approved COSTING row on the Fabric Costing page via tip-of-chain supersession
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:583-590 (supersededIds filter); 351-368 (cadRows purpose filter); frontend/src/pages/FabricCostingPage.tsx:407-413 (pickCostedPurpose priority), 928-950
findings.detail: getStyleFabrics filters returned CAD rows: `supersededIds = new Set(allCadRows.map(r => r.clonedFromCadId).filter(Boolean)); cadRows = allCadRows.filter(r => !supersededIds.has(r.id))` (fabric-costing.controller.ts:588-590) — any row referenced as another returned row's clonedFromCadId is dropped. Since order.controller's clone sets clonedFromCadId = the approved COSTING row (694), that approved row is suppressed whenever the clone is in the same result set (i.e. when no ?purpose filter is supplied — the purpose filter at 356-367 otherwise separates them). The page then auto-selects the most advanced costed tab, preferring RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION over COSTING (FabricCostingPage.tsx:409-412), landing the user on the clone, which reports orderQuantityPcs NULL (fabric-costing.controller.ts:705), processorId NULL (683-685), rateCardId NULL (700-702). The page's quantity restore filters `orderQuantityPcs != null && > 0` (FabricCostingPage.tsx:929-930) so the Qty box comes back empty.
findings.planImpact: Explains the user-visible symptom (processor/qty/rate-card blank after confirming an order) and gives an acceptance test for the fix: after PATCH status IN_PRODUCTION, GET /api/fabric-costing/style/:styleId (no purpose) must still show processor, rateCardId and a non-null orderQuantityPcs.

findings.title: Quantity does propagate to the BOM but rate does not — this is the exact divergence point
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:502 (orderQuantity), 1066/1126/1263 (totalQuantity = quantityPerGarment * orderQuantity), 1106-1108 (greigeCost/processingCost/rateCardId copied), 1185-1192; backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:1720-1722, 1759-1766, 1832
findings.detail: order-bom.service.ts:502 sets `const orderQuantity = orderItem?.totalQuantity || order.totalQuantity` — the ACTUAL order quantity — and every BOM line's totalQuantity is `quantityPerGarment * orderQuantity`. But the rate fields on the same line come from the cost sheet snapshot: `processingCost: fabricItem.processingCost` and `rateCardId: fabricItem.rateCardId` (1106-1108), or in the legacy JSON path from an arbitrary CAD row's `processingPricePerMeter` (1185-1192). MRP then copies that snapshot forward: `processingCost: bomItem.processingCost` -> requirement.processingCost and `unitPrice: processingSnapshotPrice, rateSource: 'ORDER_BOM'` (mrp.service.ts:1720-1722, 1759-1766). So meters scale with the real order while rupees-per-meter stay pinned to the manually typed costing quantity.
findings.planImpact: This is the load-bearing location for the fix, ahead of the CAD clone. A re-check inserted at order-bom.service.ts:~306 (alongside the existing validateCostSheetRates call) has both numbers in scope: orderQuantity is resolved at 502 and cadMeters/quantityPerGarment per fabric item, so `quantityMeters = quantityPerGarment * orderQuantity` is computable there and can be fed to lookupRate.

findings.title: JWO rate is the snapshot averaged, never re-looked-up at the post-netting quantity; manual JWOs take a free-typed rate
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3199-3208 and 3243-3252 (price priority), 3346-3350 (weighted average), 3453 (ratePerMeter into JWO), 3474; backend/src/controllers/job-work-order.controller.ts:232 (agreedRatePerMeter: body.agreedRate); backend/src/services/po-rate-resolver.service.ts:210-231
findings.detail: MRP JWO path: poItems[].unitPrice = `itemPrices override ?? req.unitPrice (ORDER_BOM snapshot) ?? costSheetRateMap ?? autoPriceMap ?? 0` (3199-3208 consolidate, 3243-3252 non-consolidate) — the snapshot wins whenever it is non-null. Then `totalJobValue = sum(qty * unitPrice)` and `ratePerMeter = totalJobValue / totalBillableMeters` (3346-3350), passed into buildJwoDataForProcessingPO at 3453 -> agreedRatePerMeter. The JWO quantity here is the netted `shortfall` (itemBaseQty at 3188-3191), so quantity is post-stock-netting while rate is pre-netting. The only live fallback, po-rate-resolver.service.ts resolveProcessingRate (210-231), is worse: it does `processor_rate_card.findFirst({ processorId, isActive, [printingType] }) orderBy createdAt desc` — no greigeId, no slabId, no quantity. Manual JWO creation (job-work-order.controller.ts:232) writes `agreedRatePerMeter: body.agreedRate` straight from the request body; JobWorkOrderCreateDialog.tsx:80/200/463 is a free text input with no prefill and no rate-card lookup.
findings.planImpact: Confirms the JWO half of the bug and pins the two insertion points: mrp.service.ts:3346-3350 (before ratePerMeter is frozen, where totalBillableMeters is already computed — the exact quantity to re-lookup with) and job-work-order.controller.ts:~205-232. Note po-rate-resolver.resolveProcessingRate is itself unsound and should not be reused as the re-lookup; use processor-rate-v2.service.lookupRate.

findings.title: order_items.selectedCadId is a manual width override, never auto-set at order creation, and does not drive the processing rate
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/orderProductionStatus.service.ts:293-306 (selectCad), 519-565 (getAvailableCadWidths), 571, 734; backend/src/services/orderCosting.service.ts:143-151, 219-262, 290-302, 355-395; backend/src/controllers/orderProductionStatus.controller.ts:126-132; frontend/src/components/status/OrderStatusListItem.tsx:209-223
findings.detail: selectedCadId is written only by orderProductionStatus.service.selectCad (299) and orderCosting.service.selectCadAndRecalculate (298), both driven by the user picking a width in the Order Production Status list (OrderStatusListItem.tsx:209). The candidate list (getAvailableCadWidths, 519-565) is built from `style_components[].style_fabrics[].fabricCAD` plus `style_fabrics[].fabric.widthCADs`, deduped by id and sorted by cutableWidth desc — it applies NO purpose filter, NO approvalStatus filter, and no ordering by preference beyond width. Its only consumer for money is orderCosting.calculateFabricCostsWithCad (355-395), which multiplies the CAD's cadMeters by `styleFabric.unitPrice` (the ready-fabric price) — it never reads processingPricePerMeter, and takes trims/CMT/processing totals from `style_costing[0]` (the first element, no orderBy). Separately, order_bom_items.selectedCadId (order-bom.service.ts:1112) is a different column set from the cost sheet's fabricCADId and IS what MRP reads (mrp.service.ts:1706/1789) for batch-group colour and width.
findings.planImpact: Do not route the fix through order_items.selectedCadId — it is display/quick-costing only and is null on freshly created orders. The CAD identity that matters for processor rates is order_bom_items.selectedCadId / style_costing_fabric_items.fabricCADId. Also note orderCosting's `style_costing[0]` pick is another non-deterministic 'which approved costing wins' site if the plan touches it.

findings.title: Which CAD row wins when several approved costings exist: three different rules, none of them 'the one matching this order's quantity'
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:635-658 (clones ALL matching rows); backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:1112 and 1185-1190; backend/src/services/costing.service.ts:710-741; frontend/src/pages/FabricCostingPage.tsx:928-950
findings.detail: (1) The order-confirmation clone does not choose at all — findMany at 635-658 returns every fully-approved COSTING row for the style and the loop at 673 clones each, so N approved quantity variants produce N RM clones. (2) The BOM picks by cost-sheet linkage: `selectedCadId: fabricItem.fabricCADId` (1112); the legacy JSON fallback picks `findFirst({ costingStyleId: styleId, processorId: { not: null } })` with no orderBy (1185-1190) — arbitrary. (3) The style budget sums ALL COSTING+RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION rows for the style (costing.service.ts:710-741), double-counting quantity variants. (4) The Fabric Costing page picks the row with the newest createdAt among those with orderQuantityPcs > 0 and warns 'Multiple quantity options found' (FabricCostingPage.tsx:929-951). Quantity-variant rows are exactly what the clone-on-quantity-change flow (fabric-costing.controller.ts:1007) creates, and they are grouped by orderQuantityPcs in the UI (FabricCostingOptionsPage.tsx:572-575).
findings.planImpact: The plan needs an explicit selection rule. The data model already supports 'pick the approved COSTING row whose orderQuantityPcs bracket matches this order's quantity' — orderQuantityPcs is persisted per row (schema:4626) and the options pages already group by it. Without such a rule, a re-check at order confirmation will compare against an arbitrarily chosen variant and produce false rate-change alarms.

findings.title: NEW CRITICAL: resolveProcessingRate ignores greige, slab AND quantity — and overrides the cost-sheet rate at JWO/PO time
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/po-rate-resolver.service.ts:210-232; backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3101-3112, 4990-5015, 3350, 3453
findings.detail: resolveProcessingRate queries `prisma.processor_rate_card.findFirst({ where: { processorId, isActive: true, ...(printingType ? {printingType} : {}) }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }, select: { ratePerMeter } })` (po-rate-resolver.service.ts:213-221). It filters by processorId ONLY. There is NO greigeId filter, NO laceId filter, NO slabId filter, and no quantity argument exists anywhere in RateResolutionContext (lines 8-19). It therefore returns the most-recently-created rate-card row for that processor — for an arbitrary greige and an arbitrary slab. Worse, this wins over the snapshot: mrp.service.ts:3105-3112 does `const resolved = await resolveRate({poCategory:'PROCESSING', supplierId, ...}); if (resolved.rate && resolved.rate > 0) return {key: groupKey, rate: resolved.rate}; return req.processingCost ? ... : null` — the cost-sheet-derived processingCost is only the FALLBACK. Same precedence at 4990-5008. That rate becomes poItems[].unitPrice, then the JWO's ratePerMeter as a weighted average (mrp.service.ts:3350: `totalJobValue / totalBillableMeters`), then agreedRatePerMeter (mrp.service.ts:3453 via buildJwoDataForProcessingPO, defined at 2780-2796 with `agreedRatePerMeter: seed.ratePerMeter`). Contrast with processor-rate-v2.service.ts lookupRate (877-980), which DOES do a correct quantity→slab→greige lookup but is never called from MRP/JWO — its only callers are fabric costing (fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:501) and two lookup HTTP endpoints.
findings.planImpact: Reframes the whole plan. The plan assumes JWO rates are 'snapshotted at costing time and never re-looked-up'. For MRP-generated JWOs the opposite is true: a lookup DOES run at JWO time, but it is a broken lookup that discards greige, slab and quantity, and it SUPPRESSES the (correct-greige) cost-sheet snapshot. Adding a quantity-aware re-check on top of this without fixing resolveProcessingRate will not help — the fix must make resolveProcessingRate accept greigeId/laceId + quantityMeters and delegate to processor-rate-v2.lookupRate, or the JWO re-check must bypass resolveRate entirely.

findings.title: CRITICAL: SO -> startProduction -> createWithItems creates NO order_item_costing row at all, so no costingSnapshot exists for the primary business flow
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/saleOrder.service.ts:429-440; backend/src/services/order.service.ts:109-311; backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:282-343
findings.detail: startProduction ends with `return orderService.createWithItems({...}, userId)` (saleOrder.service.ts:429-440). createWithItems (order.service.ts:109-311) contains zero references to order_item_costing, costingSnapshot, or style_costing — grep over its whole 203-line body returns nothing; the only order_item_costing reference in order.service.ts is a deleteMany at line 806. The snapshot block lives exclusively in the HTTP controller createOrder (order.controller.ts:282-343), which is wired only to POST /api/orders (routes/order.routes.ts:43-44). So orders born from a Sale Order — the flow described in the business context (Sale Order -> Order via startProduction) — have no order_item_costing, no costingSnapshot, no originalCostSheetVersion, and no estimatedCostPerPiece baseline. Note startProduction does gate on an APPROVED cost sheet (saleOrder.service.ts:352-368) but never records which one it validated against.
findings.planImpact: Claim 3's snapshot is not a reliable anchor for any fix. Any plan step that reads or refreshes order_item_costing.costingSnapshot will silently no-op for SO-originated orders. The fix must either move snapshot creation into orderService.createWithItems (covering both entry points) or stop depending on the snapshot and reconcile against order_bom instead.

findings.title: PARTIAL: claim 1 — createFromCostSheet DOES re-check processor rates, but the check is pinned to the cost sheet's own slabId, so it detects time-drift not quantity-slab-drift
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:300-337; backend/src/services/processor-rate-validation.service.ts:277-283, 329-335, 113-142
findings.detail: The claim's 'does NOT re-lookup the processor rate card' is REFUTED as written. order-bom.service.ts:306 calls `processorRateValidationService.validateCostSheetRates(input.costSheetId)` and throws a BusinessError with code RATES_OUTDATED if any item moved >=5% (lines 308-325), logging warnings otherwise (328-337). BUT the substance of the claim survives: validateCostSheetRates passes `item.rateCard?.slabId` into getCurrentProcessorRate (processor-rate-validation.service.ts:281-282 for fabric, 333-334 for lace), and getCurrentProcessorRate hard-filters `slabId: slabId || undefined` (line 131). So it asks 'has the rate for THE SLAB THE COST SHEET ALREADY PICKED changed since then?' It never asks 'given this order's actual fabric quantity, is that still the right slab?' It also never receives orderQuantity — validateCostSheetRates' only argument is costSheetId (line 203). Secondary defect: when rateCardId is null, `slabId || undefined` drops the slab filter entirely and findFirst orderBy effectiveFrom desc matches ANY slab's rate, producing a meaningless comparison.
findings.planImpact: Do not add a parallel rate-check service — extend the existing one. validateCostSheetRates needs an optional quantity parameter and must re-run the slab selection (the [min,max) logic in processor-rate-v2.service.ts:899-923) at the order's fabric quantity, then compare against the cost sheet's snapshotted processingCost. Also fix the `slabId || undefined` fallthrough so a null rateCardId is treated as unresolvable rather than as a wildcard match.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: claim 2 — copyFromPreviousOrder recalcs quantities at target qty but carries source unit prices, processing rates and rateCardId verbatim
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:1482, 1519-1520, 1535-1576, 1559-1561, 1607-1609
findings.detail: copyFromPreviousOrder starts at line 1482. Target quantity is resolved at 1520: `const newOrderQuantity = input.adjustQuantity || targetOrderItem?.totalQuantity || targetOrder.totalQuantity`. The per-item map (1535-1576) recomputes totalQuantity (1537), totalWithWastage (1539) and totalCost (1541) at the NEW quantity, but takes `const unitPrice = Number(item.unitPrice)` (1540) straight from the source row, and copies the processing economics unchanged: `greigeCost: item.greigeCost` (1559), `processingCost: item.processingCost` (1560), `rateCardId: item.rateCardId` (1561), plus processorId (1558) and sourcingStrategy (1557). There is NO call to processorRateValidationService here — unlike createFromCostSheet at line 306 — so a repeat order can be built entirely from historical rates with no staleness check whatsoever. `copiedFromOrderId: input.sourceOrderId` is set at line 1608, and sourceCostSheetId is inherited from the source BOM at 1607.
findings.planImpact: copyFromPreviousOrder is a second, completely unguarded entry point that the plan must cover. It is arguably higher-risk than createFromCostSheet because it has neither the 5% blocking gate nor any link to a current cost sheet. Same gap exists in the third BOM path (createNewVersion, order-bom.service.ts:1800-1826) which also carries sourceCostSheetId/copiedFromOrderId forward without revalidation.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: claim 4 — costingSnapshot is write-only; nothing refreshes it on re-version and nothing reconciles it against order_bom
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:296-343; backend/src/services/orderCosting.service.ts:215-252; backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:780-910; frontend/src/pages/OrderDetail.tsx:388-390
findings.detail: Repo-wide grep for `costingSnapshot` in backend/src returns only order.controller.ts:296, 338, 345, 374 — all within the single createOrder write block. It is never read, never compared, never updated. `originalCostSheetVersion` appears only at order.controller.ts:340 (write) and snapshotCreatedAt only at 339 (write). In the frontend the only consumer is a display badge: OrderDetail.tsx:388-390 renders `v{costing.originalCostSheetVersion}` with no comparison to the style's current version. orderCosting.service.ts:215-252 upserts order_item_costing on recalculation but its create/update payloads omit costingSnapshot, originalCostSheetVersion and snapshotCreatedAt entirely — so recalculation overwrites the totals while leaving a stale snapshot and a stale version number beside them. There is no trigger anywhere on style_costing re-approval/supersede that touches order_item_costing, and updateOrder (order.controller.ts:780-910) recomputes totalQuantity from the item aggregate (lines 896-902) without regenerating the order_bom or refreshing any snapshot. No code path compares order_item_costing totals to order_bom.totalMaterialCost.
findings.planImpact: Confirms the staleness gap and adds a subtlety: because orderCosting.service.ts:215-252 updates totals in place without clearing the snapshot, a refreshed order_item_costing row can present a NEW totalCostPerPiece alongside an OLD originalCostSheetVersion badge — actively misleading. Any fix should either update the version/snapshot fields in that upsert or null them when the totals are recomputed from a different base costing.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: claim 5 — orderQuantity is orderItem.totalQuantity || order.totalQuantity at line 502
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:501-502, 678, 786, 915, 1066, 1126, 1263
findings.detail: Exactly as claimed: line 501 `const orderItem = order.order_items.find((item) => item.styleId === input.styleId);` and line 502 `const orderQuantity = orderItem?.totalQuantity || order.totalQuantity;`. That single value fans out to every totalQuantity computation in the method: trims from style BOM (678), appended cost-sheet-only trims (786), JSON-fallback trims (915), relational fabric (1066), JSON fabric (1126) and lace (1263). Note the `||` (not `??`): an order item with a legitimate totalQuantity of 0 falls through to the order header total.
findings.planImpact: This is the correct single hook point for a quantity-aware rate re-check inside createFromCostSheet — the fabric quantity to slab-match on is `quantityPerGarment * orderQuantity * (1 + wastagePercent/100)` (the totalWithWastage at line 1068 / 1128), not orderQuantity in pieces.

findings.title: PARTIAL: claim 3 — snapshot is captured at order creation as described, but there is no 'processingCosts' key in it
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:296-321, 325-343; backend/prisma/schema.prisma order_item_costing model
findings.detail: The costingSnapshot object literal is built at order.controller.ts:296-321 from the latest approved, non-superseded style_costing (query at 285-292: `isApproved: true, supersededById: null, orderBy: {version: 'desc'}`). It DOES contain fabricDetails (300) and totalCostPerPiece (318), confirming those parts of the claim. It does NOT contain any field named processingCosts — the full key list is id, version, versionDate, fabricDetails, fabricTotal, trimsDetails, trimsTotal, cmtTotal, cuttingCost, stitchingCost, finishingCost, embroideryDetails, embroideryTotal, accessoriesDetails, accessoriesTotal, valueLossPercent, valueLossAmount, markupPercent, markupAmount, subtotal, totalProductCost, totalCostPerPiece, sellingPricePerPiece, profitMargin. style_costing has no processingCosts column at all. Critically, the snapshot omits the relational children where the processor economics actually live — style_costing_fabric_items (processorId, processingCost, greigeCost, rateCardId) and style_costing_lace_items are never captured. order_item_costing has a processingTotal column but the createOrder write (325-343) never sets it, so it stays at its schema default of 0.
findings.planImpact: The snapshot cannot serve as the rate baseline for any variance check — the processor rate, rateCardId and slab are simply not in it. A rate-drift comparison must read style_costing_fabric_items / style_costing_lace_items directly (as validateCostSheetRates already does), or the snapshot must be extended to include those children.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: manual JWO creation takes the rate from the request body with no rate-card lookup
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/job-work-order.controller.ts:232; backend/src/controllers/dyeing.controller.ts:1396, 1412-1414, 1563, 1595; backend/src/controllers/printing.controller.ts:1334, 1349, 1532, 1564
findings.detail: job-work-order.controller.ts:232 sets `agreedRatePerMeter: isKaaj ? 0 : body.agreedRate` — the operator-typed value, with no processor_rate_card query, no greige, no slab, no quantity check anywhere in the handler (lines 120-243). The dyeing path is the same: createProcessPO destructures agreedRatePerMeter from req.body (dyeing.controller.ts:1396), validates only that it is truthy (1412-1414), computes totalAmount = qtyBillable x agreedRatePerMeter (1563) and persists it verbatim (1595). printing.controller.ts:1334/1349/1532/1564 mirrors this. Only KAAJ_BUTTON resolves rates server-side, and from system settings rather than a rate card (job-work-order.controller.ts:179-185).
findings.planImpact: There are three distinct JWO creation surfaces needing the re-check, not one: the MRP path (mrp.service.ts:3439, broken lookup), the generic manual path (job-work-order.controller.ts:205), and the dyeing/printing process-PO paths (dyeing.controller.ts:1577, printing.controller.ts:1546). A single re-check helper should be invoked from all four call sites; scoping the plan to only the MRP path leaves the manual paths fully unguarded.

findings.title: Cost-sheet fabric rate field trace: quantity-correct slab lookup happens ONCE at costing, then only IDs are copied downstream
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:496-540; backend/prisma/schema.prisma style_costing_fabric_items (costPerMeter, greigeCost, processingCost, processorId, rateCardId, sourcingStrategy); backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:1065-1113, 1208-1235
findings.detail: Field-by-field: (1) At costing, fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:496-510 loops every DYEING/PRINTING processor calling `lookupRate({processorId, processingType, greigeId: fabric.greigeId, quantityMeters: quantityNeeded})` and keeps the cheapest — this is the only quantity-aware slab match in the chain (slab selection at processor-rate-v2.service.ts:899-923). (2) The winner is persisted to style_costing_fabric_items as processingCost (rate/m), greigeCost, processorId, rateCardId, costPerMeter (all-in). (3) createFromCostSheet's relational branch (order-bom.service.ts:1010-1114) copies them straight across: unitPrice = Number(fabricItem.costPerMeter) (1076), processorId (1106), greigeCost (1107), processingCost (1108), rateCardId (1109) — pure field copy, no lookup. (4) The JSON fallback branch (1117-1236) reads fabricDetails[].fabricRate/greigeCost/processingCost/rateCardId, or reconstructs from fabric_width_cad (1180-1195) when sourcingStrategy is missing; unitPrice = `fabric.fabricRate || greigeCost || 0` (1210). (5) MRP snapshots bomItem.processingCost onto material_requirements.processingCost (mrp.service.ts:1711, 1722, 1746, 1759) — which is then overridden at JWO time by the broken resolveProcessingRate. Note the contradictory in-code comments: line 1010 treats the relational branch as preferred, while line 1116 states 'Fallback to JSON fabricDetails (primary path — relational table is not populated)'.
findings.planImpact: The re-lookup helper should mirror fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:501 (same lookupRate signature, same greigeId source) so costing and re-check agree by construction. Also resolve the 1010-vs-1116 comment contradiction before touching either branch — the plan must patch BOTH the relational and JSON fabric branches, since it is unclear from the code which is live in production.

findings.title: No versioning or staleness guard exists between style_costing.version and order_bom.sourceCostSheetId
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:1395, 1607, 1823; backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3115, 4987; backend/prisma/schema.prisma style_costing (version, versionDate, supersededById, approvalStatus)
findings.detail: style_costing carries version (Int @default(1)), versionDate, versionReason and supersededById with indexes on [styleId, version] and [supersededById]. order_bom stores only sourceCostSheetId — no version column, no snapshot of the version it was built from. All three BOM creation paths write it and never validate it: createFromCostSheet `sourceCostSheetId: input.costSheetId` (1395), copyFromPreviousOrder inherits `sourceBOM.sourceCostSheetId` (1607), createNewVersion inherits `currentBOM.sourceCostSheetId` (1823). Both MRP consumers read it purely as a lookup key with no freshness test: mrp.service.ts:3115 and 4987 both do `const costSheetId = (req as any).orderBom?.sourceCostSheetId ?? null` then feed it to resolveRate. Nothing anywhere checks whether that cost sheet has since been superseded (supersededById != null) or whether a higher-version approved sheet exists for the style. The only related guard is the 5% rate check at order-bom.service.ts:306, which validates rates but not sheet version.
findings.planImpact: Supports adding a version/staleness guard, and shows where: order_bom needs a sourceCostSheetVersion column (or a join-time supersededById check) so createFromCostSheet, copyFromPreviousOrder and both MRP read sites can detect that the BOM was built from a superseded sheet. Cheapest interim guard: at BOM creation, reject or warn when the chosen style_costing has supersededById != null.

findings.title: PARTIAL: material_requirements.unitPrice IS snapshotted from order_bom_items with rateSource 'ORDER_BOM' — but the cited lines 3345-3350 are the wrong location
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:1583-1584, 1681-1685, 1714-1716, 1722, 1758-1760, 1769, 1791-1792 (snapshot construction); 1956-1958, 1994-1996, 2081-2083, 2121-2123 (DB persist); backend/prisma/schema.prisma:3795-3797
findings.detail: The snapshot is real and pervasive. For GREIGE_PROCESSED lines MRP creates TWO requirements from one BOM item: the GREIGE one takes `unitPrice: greigeSnapshotPrice` (= bomItem.greigeCost ?? bomItem.unitPrice, line 1681-1685) with `rateSource: greigeSnapshotPrice != null ? 'ORDER_BOM' : null` (1716); the PROCESSING one takes `unitPrice: processingSnapshotPrice` (= Number(bomItem.processingCost), line 1722) with the same rateSource literal (1760). Standard lines use bomItem.unitPrice (1769/1791-1792). These are written to material_requirements at 1994-1996 (MATERIAL create), 2121-2123 (PROCESSING create) and re-written on recalc at 1956-1958 / 2081-2083. Schema columns exist: `unitPrice Decimal? @db.Decimal(12,4)`, `rateSource String?` documented as 'ORDER_BOM' | 'COST_SHEET' | 'SUPPLIER_PRICE' | 'RATE_CARD' | 'MANUAL', `orderBomItemId String?` (schema.prisma:3795-3797). Lines 3345-3350 are something else entirely: jwoUom / totalJobValue / value-weighted ratePerMeter for the JWO.
findings.planImpact: Plan must target lines 1714-1760 / 2081-2123 for any re-snapshot logic, not 3345-3350. Note there are TWO snapshots per greige-processed BOM line (greige price and processing price) that diverge independently. rateSource already has a 'RATE_CARD' enum value defined but never written by any code path — a re-lookup can set it without a migration.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: requirement formula is orderQty x qtyPerUnit x (1 + wastage/100), then divided by (1 - shrinkage) for greige
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:1209-1219 (formula), 1214 (comment states it verbatim), 1252-1263 (shrinkage gross-up), 1211 (orderQuantity = orderItem.totalQuantity)
findings.detail: `const baseRequiredDecimal = multiplyCurrency(orderQuantity, quantityPerUnit); const wastageAmountDecimal = baseRequiredDecimal.times(toCurrency(wastagePercent).dividedBy(100)); const totalRequiredDecimal = baseRequiredDecimal.plus(wastageAmountDecimal);` at 1216-1218. orderQuantity is `orderItem.totalQuantity` (1211) — the ACTUAL production order quantity, entirely independent of the manually-typed orderQuantityPcs used at costing. For GREIGE_PROCESSED/LANDED_GREIGE with a shrinkage % (1235-1263), totalRequired is then grossed up via calculateGreigeQuantity(need, 0, shrinkagePercent) = need / (1 - s/100).
findings.planImpact: Confirms the divergence mechanism: the quantity axis is order-driven while the rate axis is costing-driven. Any re-lookup must decide whether to use totalRequired (greige basis) or shortfall x (1-s) (billable/fabric basis) — see finding on itemBaseQty.

findings.title: PARTIAL: the JWO builder does set agreedRatePerMeter from the snapshot with zero rate-card re-lookup — but the function is named buildJwoDataForProcessingPO, not seedToJwoCreateInput
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:2780-2804 (function), 2796 (`agreedRatePerMeter: seed.ratePerMeter`), 2797 (`isRateTbd: false`), 3346-3350 (seed.ratePerMeter derivation), 3200-3208 / 3244-3252 (item.unitPrice = snapshot), 3439-3465 (call site)
findings.detail: No symbol `seedToJwoCreateInput` exists in the repo. The real function is `export function buildJwoDataForProcessingPO(seed: ProcessingJwoSeed, jobWorkNumber: string)` at 2780, and line 2796 is `agreedRatePerMeter: seed.ratePerMeter`. seed.ratePerMeter is computed at 3346-3350 as `totalJobValue / totalBillableMeters` where totalJobValue = SUM(item.quantity x item.unitPrice) and item.unitPrice comes from the price cascade at 3200-3208 (consolidate) / 3244-3252 (non-consolidate): `itemPrices?.[key] ?? itemPrices?.[req.materialId] ?? snapshotPrice ?? costSheetRateMap.get(key) ?? costSheetRateMap.get(req.materialId) ?? autoPriceMap.get(req.materialId) ?? 0`. snapshotPrice = `req.unitPrice` (3200/3244), i.e. the costing-time processingCost. `lookupRate` is never imported into mrp.service.ts — grep for callers shows only fabric-costing.controller.ts:837 and fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:501.
findings.planImpact: Insert point for a JWO-creation re-lookup is mrp.service.ts around 3346-3350 (before buildJwoDataForProcessingPO is called at 3441), not inside the builder — the builder is a pure mapper also used by a backfill script and has no DB access.

findings.title: REFUTED: MRP does NOT net the PROCESSING requirement (the one that becomes the JWO) against stock — it is hard-coded to the full quantity
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:1739-1741 (`availableStock: 0, allocatedFromStock: 0, shortfall: totalRequired` with comment "Processing doesn't have stock"), 2070-2071 and 2103-2104 (persisted as 0/0), 4853-4855 (convert path, same)
findings.detail: Stock netting is real but applies ONLY to MATERIAL requirements. The netting block is mrp.service.ts:1275-1421 and reads four different sources: greige_stock aggregate filtered `status:'AVAILABLE', quantityAvailable:{gt:0}, processorId:null` (1278-1289); fabric_stock aggregate with cutableWidth +/-0.5in tolerance (1310-1318) plus an any-width fallback (1321-1328) and a no-width branch (1358-1365); lace_stock (1381-1388); and getDerivedOnHand(materialId) for generic trims (1409). All of these write into `shortfall` for the MATERIAL/GREIGE requirement created at 1688-1718 or 1771-1794. The PROCESSING sibling created at 1729-1765 explicitly sets availableStock: 0 / allocatedFromStock: 0 / shortfall: totalRequired (1739-1741). So the '2500m costed / 1500m ordered / 700m JWO after stock netting' narrative is wrong for the main GREIGE_PROCESSED path: the JWO quantity is NOT reduced by greige-on-hand.
findings.planImpact: The plan's stated bug mechanism is wrong for the dominant path. The real quantity-divergence drivers are (i) orderItem.totalQuantity vs the manually-typed costing orderQuantityPcs, (ii) the wizard's itemQuantities override, (iii) batch-group consolidation, (iv) partial-JWO child splits. A fix justified purely by 'stock netting shrinks the JWO' will not match observed data.

findings.title: CONFIRMED (narrow path): convertToGreigeProcessing DOES produce a stock-netted JWO quantity
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:4703-4880; 4716 (`const shortfallQty = Number(requirement.shortfall)`), 4758-4771 (shrinkage gross-up), 4851-4855 (processing req gets that qty), 4865-4866 (`unitPrice: data.processingCost ?? null, rateSource: 'MANUAL'`)
findings.detail: This is the ONE path where the claim-3 story holds. convertToGreigeProcessing starts from the parent MATERIAL requirement's already-stock-netted `shortfall` (4716), grosses it up for shrinkage, and creates GREIGE + PROCESSING requirements at that reduced quantity. Worse for costing: the processing price is whatever the user typed in the dialog (`data.processingCost`) and rateSource is hard-coded 'MANUAL' (4866) — there is no rate-card consultation at all, at any quantity.
findings.planImpact: convertToGreigeProcessing is a second, independent insertion point for a rate lookup and is arguably the highest-value one (it currently accepts a free-typed rate). It also already has processorId + greigeId + the exact quantity in scope at line 4760, so a lookupRate call is trivial there.

findings.title: PARTIAL: createDyeJob takes agreedRatePerMeter from req.body with no lookup — but it has NO isRateTbd flag; isRateTbd lives only in createProcessPO at ~1397/1596
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/dyeing.controller.ts:891-965 (createDyeJob), 897-908 (destructure, no isRateTbd), 941-960 (create data, no isRateTbd); 1381-1409 (createProcessPO destructure incl. `isRateTbd = false` at 1397), 1412-1414 (validation), 1595-1596 (`agreedRatePerMeter, isRateTbd,`)
findings.detail: createDyeJob is at 891-965 exactly as cited, and line 956 is a bare `agreedRatePerMeter,` shorthand straight from req.body — no rate-card call. But createDyeJob never mentions isRateTbd, so the JWO row falls back to the schema default `isRateTbd Boolean @default(false)` (schema.prisma:6841). createProcessPO (1381-1732) is the MRP-adjacent path and is the one with the TBD flag; note its validation `if (!qtySentMeters || !sentWidthInches || !agreedRatePerMeter)` at 1412 is falsy-based, so a rate of 0 is REJECTED there even when isRateTbd is true — the TBD flag is unreachable via that guard. The file imports no rate-lookup symbol: grep for lookupRate across dyeing.controller.ts returns nothing.
findings.planImpact: Two distinct create paths need the fix, and the isRateTbd escape hatch only exists on one of them (and is currently broken by the falsy guard at 1412). A rate re-check must be skippable when isRateTbd is set, which means the 1412 guard has to change too.

findings.title: PARTIAL: the sentDate lock at 990-992 blocks the WHOLE update, not just the rate, and only exists on /jobs/:id — Process POs have no update route at all
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/dyeing.controller.ts:990-992 (`if (existing.sentDate) throw new ValidationError('Cannot update a job that has already been sent to mill')`), 1003 (`if (agreedRatePerMeter !== undefined) updateData.agreedRatePerMeter = ...`); backend/src/routes/dyeing.routes.ts:194 (only PUT), 80-109 (process-pos routes: GET/POST/DELETE + action POSTs, no PUT/PATCH); backend/src/controllers/printing.controller.ts:931-933 (identical mirror)
findings.detail: The guard is real but is a blanket update block, not a rate-specific lock, and it fires on sentDate for every field. It lives in updateDyeJob (968-1013), which routes from `PUT /jobs/:id` (dyeing.routes.ts:194) — the lab-dip dye-job flow. Process POs / MRP-generated JWOs have NO update endpoint whatsoever (dyeing.routes.ts:80-109 and printing.routes.ts:79-108 expose only get/create/delete/send/receive/quality-check/update-stock/return-unprocessed), and job-work-order.routes.ts:27-73 has no PUT/PATCH either. So for the JWOs the plan actually cares about, agreedRatePerMeter is immutable from the instant of creation, not from issue.
findings.planImpact: 'Re-check rate at JWO creation' is effectively the LAST chance to get the number right — there is no later correction endpoint. Also means a re-check cannot be retrofitted as an update hook; it must be inline in the create paths.

findings.title: A post-issue rate channel already exists and bypasses the sentDate lock: actualRate at Quality Check
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/dyeing.controller.ts:1133-1160 (qualityCheck writes actualRate), 2009-2035 (qualityCheckProcessPO writes actualRate), 1204 (`Number(existing.actualRate || existing.agreedRatePerMeter)`); backend/src/services/grn.service.ts:2898 (`processingQC?.actualRate ?? jobWorkOrder.actualRate ?? jobWorkOrder.agreedRatePerMeter ?? 0`), 714; backend/prisma/schema.prisma:6853 (`actualRate Decimal? @db.Decimal(10,2)`)
findings.detail: job_work_orders.actualRate is settable AFTER dispatch via POST /process-pos/:id/quality-check (routes 97-102) and is preferred over agreedRatePerMeter everywhere costs are actually consumed (grn.service.ts:714, 2898; dyeing.controller.ts:1204, 2079; printing.controller.ts:1154, 2055). So the 'rate locks at issue' framing is incomplete — there is an unaudited, unvalidated override that lands after the goods are gone.
findings.planImpact: actualRate is a ready-made 'corrected rate' column. If the plan wants a costedRate-vs-actual variance report, actualRate already holds the second number; what is missing is the ORIGIN of the first one (which slab/rate-card the agreed rate came from).

findings.title: (a) One requirement row yields one JWO by construction; partial coverage forks a CHILD requirement, which is what produces the second JWO
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3484-3496 (link creation), 3501-3515 (coverage check), 3517-3555 (child requirement create with splitFromId, copying unitPrice/rateSource verbatim at 3550-3551), 3555 (parent shortfall reduced to `covered`); backend/prisma/schema.prisma:3866 (`@@unique([requirementId, jobWorkOrderId])`)
findings.detail: The MRP JWO path links each requirement once (3486-3493, allocatedQuantity = item.quantity or an even split when a poItem bundles several requirements), then for each requirement computes `remainder = shortfall - covered` in greige basis (3508-3511) and, if remainder > 0.01, mints a NEW material_requirements row with splitFromId = parent (3517-3554) and truncates the parent's shortfall (3555). Critically, line 3550-3551 copies `unitPrice: req.unitPrice, rateSource: req.rateSource` onto the child — so the second JWO inherits the SAME frozen costing-time rate at a strictly smaller quantity. The schema's unique constraint permits multiple JWOs per requirement, and updateJwoReceivedQuantity aggregates across `allLinks` for one requirementId (4126-4138), so the design anticipates it; the only way a single row gets a second link today is JWO cancellation, which reverts status to PO_REQUIRED and deletes the link (job-work-order.controller.ts:1239-1247).
findings.planImpact: A rate lookup at JWO creation must ALSO run on the child-split path (3517-3554), otherwise the split silently propagates the stale rate. And because each JWO knows only its own slice, the natural lookup quantity is per-JWO — which means two JWOs from one requirement can legitimately land in two different slabs and the sum of their costs will not equal the single-slab cost that was quoted.

findings.title: (a) A JWO can bundle MULTIPLE requirements at different rates and stores only a value-weighted average — so 'the quantity for a rate lookup' is ambiguous
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3333-3356 (MRP-15 comment + weighted average), 3319 (`totalBillableMeters` = sum of all poItems), 3338-3344 (unit-mixing guard), 3351-3356 (warn when rates differ), 3490-3491 (allocatedQuantity split evenly when a poItem carries >1 requirement)
findings.detail: `const ratePerMeter = totalBillableMeters > 0 ? toNumber(roundToCent(totalJobValue / totalBillableMeters)) : 0;` (3350). job_work_orders holds one qty and one rate, so a JWO bundling three requirements at three different processingCosts collapses to a single blended number, with only a logWarn (3352-3355). The only hard guard is on mixed UNITS (3338-3344), not mixed rates.
findings.planImpact: Directly answers the question 'what quantity would a rate lookup even use'. Three candidates exist in scope at 3319-3350: totalBillableMeters (billable/fabric out, what the processor invoices), totalGreigeMeters (3320-3323, what is physically issued), or per-poItem item.quantity. Doing it per-item and re-blending preserves the existing weighted-average contract; doing it once on totalBillableMeters is simpler but changes per-item line values. Note also that a slab lookup on the BUNDLE quantity gives a cheaper rate than per-item lookups — which is exactly what FabricCostingPage already does at costing time (see the batch-group finding), so per-item lookup at JWO time would systematically contradict the cost sheet.

findings.title: (b) job_work_orders has NO rate-audit fields to reuse — only agreedRatePerMeter, isRateTbd, actualRate
findings.evidence: backend/prisma/schema.prisma:6804-6912 (full model) — 6840 agreedRatePerMeter, 6841 isRateTbd, 6853 actualRate, 6872-6878 subtotal/gstRate/tax fields, 6894 declaredValue; relations block 6914-6945 has no processor_rate_card relation; grep for 'rate' over 6804-6965 returns only those
findings.detail: There is no quotedRate, no costedRate, no rateSource, no rateCardId, no slabId, no rateLookedUpAt on job_work_orders. The nearest analogues elsewhere DO exist and are the natural donors of the pattern: order_bom_items.rateCardId with relation `rateCard processor_rate_card? @relation("bom_item_rate_card")` (schema.prisma:245, 280); style_costing_fabric_items.rateCardId + relation (2046, 2058); material_requirements.rateSource + unitPrice + orderBomItemId (3795-3797). job_work_order_components has `rate` and `rateAtIssue Decimal? @db.Decimal(12,4) // D4: Immutable rate snapshot at issue` (6993-6994) but this is the MATERIAL cost, not the processing rate: job-work-issuance.service.ts:473-490 fills it from `row.purchaseCost ?? row.weightedAvgCost` with `isChargeable: false // principal's free-issue material`, and only when lots.length > 1 (470).
findings.planImpact: New columns on job_work_orders ARE required — nothing is reusable. Minimum viable set mirroring existing conventions: `rateCardId String?` + relation (copy order_bom_items:280), `rateSource String?` (copy material_requirements:3796, whose documented enum already includes 'RATE_CARD'), and `costedRatePerMeter Decimal? @db.Decimal(10,2)` to hold the superseded snapshot. Do NOT try to overload job_work_order_components.rateAtIssue — it means material value and feeds declaredValue/e-way bill (6994, 489) and GRN valuation (grn.service.ts:2911).

findings.title: (c) JWO seed quantityMeters = sum of per-item billable qty divided back through each item's shrinkage; qtyBillable is the un-divided sum
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3188-3191 (itemBaseQty), 3213/3218/3257 (poItem.quantity), 3232-3235 & 3254 (itemQuantities override REPLACES the qty), 3314-3323 (totalBillableMeters / totalGreigeMeters), 3326-3331 (impliedShrinkage), 3449-3450 (`qtyMeters` / `qtyBillable`), 2758-2760 (processingBillableQty), 2735-2751 (resolveProcessingShrinkagePercent)
findings.detail: Chain: `itemBaseQty(req) = processingBillableQty(Number(req.shortfall), resolveProcessingShrinkagePercent(req))` = shortfall x (1 - s) for PROCESSING (3188-3191). That becomes poItem.quantity (3218 summed per group, or 3257 per requirement), which the wizard can REPLACE wholesale via itemQuantities (3234 `group.quantity = Number(overrideQty)` / 3257). Then `totalBillableMeters = SUM(item.quantity)` (3319) and `totalGreigeMeters = SUM(divideByShrinkage(item.quantity, itemShrinkage(item)))` (3320-3323). Finally seed `qtyMeters: roundToCent(totalGreigeMeters)` (3449, commented "greige to issue") and `qtyBillable: roundToCent(totalBillableMeters)` (3450, "fabric the processor bills for"). expectedShrinkage is back-derived from the two totals (3326-3331). Billing consumes qtyBillable: job-work-order.doc-data.ts:390 `multiplyCurrency(jwo.qtyBillable ?? jwo.qtySentMeters, jwo.agreedRatePerMeter)`.
findings.planImpact: qtyBillable (not qtySentMeters) is the quantity the rate is actually multiplied by, so a slab lookup keyed on qtySentMeters would be off by the shrinkage factor (~5-10%) and can straddle a slab boundary. Use totalBillableMeters at 3319. Also note the itemQuantities override at 3234/3254 means the operator can silently move the JWO into a different slab from the review screen with no rate consequence today.

findings.title: The only rate re-check that exists (order_bom creation) pins the ORIGINAL slab, so it detects price drift but is blind to quantity-slab drift
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:304-337 (blocking validation); backend/src/services/processor-rate-validation.service.ts:203-298, especially 277-283 (`getCurrentProcessorRate(item.processorId, item.greigeId, null, item.rateCard?.processingType || 'DYEING', item.rateCard?.slabId)`), 113-142 (query filters `slabId: slabId || undefined`), 98-102 + BLOCKING/WARNING thresholds
findings.detail: createOrderBom calls validateCostSheetRates and hard-blocks at >=5% change (order-bom.service.ts:306-325, throwing 'RATES_OUTDATED'), warning-logs smaller drifts (328-337). But the comparison passes `item.rateCard?.slabId` into getCurrentProcessorRate (277-283 -> 131), which pins the query to the SAME slab the cost sheet chose. It answers 'did the processor change the price of slab X?' It never asks 'is the order still in slab X?'. Since the order quantity is not even an input to this function, a 2500m-costed / 700m-actual job passes validation cleanly while sitting in a completely different slab.
findings.planImpact: This is the single most important finding for the plan. There is already a validation hook wired into the exact spot the plan wants ('rate re-check at order confirmation') — it just asks the wrong question. Extending validateCostSheetRates to accept a quantity and re-derive the slab (mirroring lookupRate's slab-matching at processor-rate-v2.service.ts:899-923) reuses the existing blocking/warning UX, error code, and frontend handling instead of adding a parallel mechanism.

findings.title: The costing-time rate is looked up at cadMeters x manually-typed orderQuantityPcs, and rateCardId is copied to the BOM unchanged
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/FabricCostingPage.tsx:352 (`const [orderQuantity, setOrderQuantity] = useState<number>(0)`), 1130-1132 (`rowQuantityMeters = row.cadMeters * rowQty`), 1182-1188 (lookupRate call), 1434 (persists orderQuantityPcs); backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:819-843; backend/src/services/processor-rate-v2.service.ts:877-980; backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:1065-1068, 1076, 1107-1109; backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4626 (fabric_width_cad.orderQuantityPcs), 2046 (style_costing_fabric_items.rateCardId)
findings.detail: lookupRate slab-matches on `minQuantity: { lte: quantityMeters }, maxQuantity: { gt: quantityMeters }` half-open (processor-rate-v2.service.ts:899-911) with a highest-slab fallback (914-923), then finds the rate card for (processor, processingType, greigeId, slabId) (930-949). The quantity fed in is cadMeters x the user-typed pcs. order-bom.service.ts then computes quantities from the REAL order (`totalQuantity = quantityPerGarment * orderQuantity`, 1066, where orderQuantity = orderItem.totalQuantity ?? order.totalQuantity, line 502) while copying prices unchanged: `greigeCost`, `processingCost`, `rateCardId: fabricItem.rateCardId` (1107-1109). The quantity is re-derived; the rate is not.
findings.planImpact: Confirms the exact seam. order_bom_items.rateCardId (schema 245) is the breadcrumb that makes a re-lookup cheap: it identifies the processor + processingType + printingType + greige + the ORIGINAL slab, so a downstream re-lookup only needs the new quantity. The plan should thread orderBomItem.rateCard through — mrp.service.ts already includes it (3291-3293, 2502, 2738-2743) so the relation is loaded in the JWO path.

findings.title: The PROCESSING fallback resolver picks a rate card ignoring BOTH greige and slab — newest card for the processor wins
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/po-rate-resolver.service.ts:210-232 (`resolveProcessingRate`); called from backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3102-3112 (generation) and 4995-5014 (preview)
findings.detail: `prisma.processor_rate_card.findFirst({ where: { processorId: ctx.supplierId, isActive: true, ...(ctx.printingType ? { printingType } : {}) }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }, select: { ratePerMeter: true } })` — no greigeId filter, no slabId filter, no quantity. Whatever rate row that processor most recently created is returned as the price. This is the value written into costSheetRateMap for PROCESSING requirements (mrp.service.ts:3108, 5005) and is the fallback when the ORDER_BOM snapshot is null (3204/3248 and 5126). It also feeds the review-screen preview the operator approves.
findings.planImpact: Fixing only the snapshot path leaves this equally-wrong fallback live for every legacy/manual requirement with a null unitPrice. The plan should replace resolveProcessingRate's body with a real lookupRate(processorId, processingType, printingType, greigeId, quantity) call — it already receives supplierId and printingType and can reach greigeId via req.materials.greigeId (available at mrp.service.ts:5024).

findings.title: PurchaseOrderForm hard-codes quantityMeters=1 when auto-filling the processing rate, guaranteeing the lowest slab
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/PurchaseOrderForm.tsx:794-811 (`lookupProcessingRate(newItem.tempId, greige.id, 1)` at 810, with orderedQuantity: '1' at 801), 813-852 (the lookup)
findings.detail: When a greige line is added to a processing PO the form immediately calls the slab lookup with quantity 1, writing that rate into item.unitPrice (831). There is no re-lookup wired to the quantity field afterwards — grep shows lookupProcessingRate is only invoked at 810.
findings.planImpact: Independent instance of the same bug class, in a path the plan does not mention. Cheap to fix in the same change; also a useful precedent that the frontend must re-trigger lookups on quantity change, which the JWO create form will need too.

findings.title: ProcessPOCreateForm already calls lookupRate but throws away ratePerMeter, using only shrinkagePercent
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/processing/ProcessPOCreateForm.tsx:295-321 (effect), 302-307 (call with `qtySentMeters || 1`), 308-313 (only `rate.shrinkagePercent` is consumed), 94 + 113 (agreedRatePerMeter state initialised/reset to 0), 1090-1108 (manual input + TBD checkbox), 396/411 (sent to API)

findings.planImpact: Lowest-friction frontend win: the lookup call, its dependency array (already keyed on qtySentMeters), and its error handling all exist. Populating agreedRatePerMeter + surfacing slabLabel is a few lines at 308-313. Backend enforcement is still needed since createProcessPO trusts req.body (dyeing.controller.ts:1595).

findings.title: Manual createProcessPO closes a linked MRP requirement in full even when the JWO covers only part of it — no child split, unlike the MRP path
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/dyeing.controller.ts:1622-1643 (link loop), 1624-1627 (unconditional flip to PO_GENERATED), 1635-1638 (`allocatedQuantity: Math.min(shortfall x (1-s), qtyBillable)`); contrast backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3501-3555 (child split); backend/src/controllers/printing.controller.ts:1598 (same pattern)
