The MRP-generated path does the opposite (mrp.service.ts:3515 `if (remainder <= 0.01) continue;` then creates a child at 3517).
findings.planImpact: Asymmetry to be aware of when reasoning about 'multiple JWOs per requirement': via the manual path a requirement is consumed by one partial JWO and the balance is silently lost, so a rate re-check there has no second bite. Also means requirement-level cost reconciliation will under-report on manually-created JWOs.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: lookupRate signature, half-open slab match, returns ratePerMeter — but processorId is OPTIONAL and there is a silent fallback to the TOP slab
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/processor-rate-v2.service.ts:877-980; query type at backend/src/types/processor-rate-v2.types.ts:132-157; interval at :899-911; fallback at :913-923
findings.detail: `export async function lookupRate(query: RateLookupQuery): Promise<RateLookupResult | null>` (line 877) destructures `{ processorId, processingType, printingType, greigeId, quantityMeters }` (line 878). Slab match is `minQuantity: { lte: quantityMeters }, maxQuantity: { gt: quantityMeters }` — half-open [min,max), with an explicit comment citing bug-hunt BH-0329 (lines 904-910). It returns `ratePerMeter` (line 975). THREE caveats the claim omits: (1) `processorId` is OPTIONAL in RateLookupQuery (types line 133) and when absent lookupRate silently substitutes the supplier with code `SYSTEM_DEFAULT` (lines 885-895); (2) when no slab matches, it does NOT return null — it falls back to `orderBy: { maxQuantity: 'desc' }`, i.e. the TOP slab (lines 913-923). That fallback is documented as "for quantities exceeding max slab range" but it also fires when quantity is BELOW the lowest slab's minQuantity, handing a tiny quantity the best volume rate; (3) the rate-card `findFirst` at lines 942-949 has NO orderBy, so if two isActive rows exist for the same (processor, type, printingType, greige, slab) cell the pick is DB-order dependent — and the unique key deliberately allows multiple rows per cell (schema.prisma:2862 includes effectiveFrom).
findings.planImpact: A re-lookup helper must decide what to do when the new (smaller) JWO quantity falls BELOW the lowest slab: today it silently gets the cheapest top-slab rate rather than erroring. Also, any new lookupRateWithSlab must keep processorId REQUIRED at the JWO/order hop — the SYSTEM_DEFAULT fallback would silently price against a phantom processor.

findings.title: PARTIAL: fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:501 does call lookupRate with quantityNeeded = cadMeters × orderQuantity — but this file is NOT the code path the Fabric Costing page uses
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:143, :152, :368-372, :494-511; vs. real page path frontend/src/pages/FabricCostingPage.tsx:1131-1188 → backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:819-843 → processor-rate-v2.service.ts:877
findings.detail: In fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts, `quantityNeeded` traces as: calculateFabricCost receives `{cadMeters, orderQuantity}` (line 115), computes `totalMetersNeeded = multiplyCurrency(cadMeters, orderQuantity || 1)` (line 143), passes it as the `quantityNeeded` arg of calculateGreigeProcessingCost (line 152, param at line 370), which passes it as `quantityMeters` to lookupRate (line 505). So yes: meters-per-piece × pieces. BUT: (a) the `|| 1` fallback (line 143) means a missing/zero orderQuantity silently looks up the rate for ONE METRE — lowest slab, worst rate; (b) this service is only reached via POST /api/fabric-costing/calculate and /batch-calculate (controller lines 18-52, 58-105), whose only caller is the cost-sheet comparison modal frontend/src/components/cost-sheet/FabricCostingRow.tsx:71-77 — NOT the Fabric Costing page; (c) it ignores the user's chosen processor entirely, looping every DYEING/PRINTING processor and keeping the cheapest rate (lines 495-511). The REAL costing-time lookup is the frontend calling POST /api/fabric-costing/lookup-rate (FabricCostingPage.tsx:1182-1188) with `quantityMeters = row.cadMeters * (row.rowQuantity || orderQuantity)` (line 1131-1132), where `row.cadMeters` is per-piece consumption (cadAverage), resolved backend-side at fabric-costing.controller.ts:636-651 as `cadRow.cadAverage`, or if null, `(cadMeters + layerMargin) / sum(sizeBreakdowns.quantity)`.
findings.planImpact: A fix that only patches fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts will miss the actual costing path. Both entry points must be covered: the controller endpoint at fabric-costing.controller.ts:819 (page path) and the service loop at fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:501 (modal path). Note the size-breakdown derivation at controller:641-649 means cadAverage itself can shift if size breakdowns change.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: FabricCostingPage orderQuantity is manual state at :352, typed into a plain Input, and saved as orderQuantityPcs at :1434
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/FabricCostingPage.tsx:352, :1942-1949, :1434, :930-948; persisted at backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4626
findings.detail: `const [orderQuantity, setOrderQuantity] = useState<number>(0)` (line 352), bound to `<Input type="number" onChange={(e) => setOrderQuantity(parseInt(e.target.value) || 0)}>` (lines 1942-1949). Save sends `orderQuantityPcs: row.rowQuantity ?? orderQuantity ?? 0` (line 1434) — note a PER-ROW override `rowQuantity` exists and wins over the global. Stored to `fabric_width_cad.orderQuantityPcs Int?` (schema.prisma:4626). On reload the page rehydrates the global from the MOST RECENT saved row by createdAt (lines 928-948) and only if the user hasn't typed one (line 943). Changing the quantity does NOT overwrite the row: quantityChanged triggers CLONE mode (lines 1396-1404), creating a NEW fabric_width_cad row and preserving the old costing option.
findings.planImpact: Confirms the plan's premise for the costing hop. Also means "the costed quantity" is per-CAD-row (orderQuantityPcs), not per-style — a re-check must compare against the specific fabric_width_cad row's own orderQuantityPcs, and the clone behaviour means several rows for the same fabric can carry different costed quantities simultaneously.

findings.title: (a) CONFIRMED: lookupRate ALREADY returns full slab metadata (slabId, slabLabel, minQuantity, maxQuantity) end-to-end — do not add lookupRateWithSlab
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/processor-rate-v2.service.ts:947, :971-974; type backend/src/types/processor-rate-v2.types.ts:149-152; frontend type frontend/src/types/fabricCosting.types.ts:303-318; grep for "lookupRateWithSlab" returns zero matches repo-wide
findings.detail: The rate-card include already selects `slab: { select: { id, slabLabel, minQuantity, maxQuantity } }` (line 947) and the return object emits `slabId`, `slabLabel`, `minQuantity: Number(rateCard.slab.minQuantity)`, `maxQuantity: Number(rateCard.slab.maxQuantity)` (lines 971-974), plus `shrinkagePercent` (line 977) and `screenCostPerScreen` (line 978). RateLookupResult declares all of these (types 141-157) and the frontend ProcessorRateLookup mirrors them verbatim (fabricCosting.types.ts:303-318). So a caller can already answer "is quantity X still inside the slab this row was priced in?" with one existing call. What is missing is not the data but the STORAGE of the boundaries at costing time: FabricCostingPage keeps only `slabLabel` and `rateCardId` from the result (lines 1212-1224) and drops minQuantity/maxQuantity; fabric_width_cad has `rateCardId` (schema.prisma:4665) but no slab columns — the boundaries are recoverable only by joining rateCard.slabId → processor_quantity_slabs.
findings.planImpact: Delete any "add lookupRateWithSlab" step. The re-check is: read the stored rateCardId → its slab's min/max, compare to the new quantity, and call the EXISTING lookupRate with the new quantity if it fell out of band. No new lookup function, no schema change needed to detect the drift.

findings.title: (b) PARTIAL: rate cards DO carry effectiveFrom/effectiveTo/supersededById/previousRateValue — but lookupRate filters ONLY on isActive, never on date
findings.evidence: backend/prisma/schema.prisma:2839-2845, :2862, :2869-2870; lookupRate filter backend/src/services/processor-rate-v2.service.ts:930-943; supersede logic :126-166; date-aware helpers backend/src/services/processor-rate-validation.service.ts:125-142, :170-187
findings.detail: processor_rate_card has full versioning: `effectiveFrom DateTime @default(now())`, `effectiveTo DateTime?` ("null = currently active"), `supersededById`, `previousRateValue`, `changeReasonCode`, `changeNotes` (schema lines 2840-2845), a self-relation RateHistory (2859-2860), effectiveFrom in the unique key (2862) and indexes on it (2869-2870). There is NO expiry/validUntil concept beyond effectiveTo, and nothing auto-expires. lookupRate's rate-card filter is `{processorId, processingType, greigeId, slabId, isActive: true}` (+printingType) — no effectiveFrom/effectiveTo predicate at all (lines 930-943). In practice this is usually equivalent because updateRateWithHistory sets `effectiveTo: now, isActive: false` together in one transaction (lines 130-136), but the two columns are written independently elsewhere: saveProcessorRateMatrix selects its "active" rows by `effectiveTo: null` only, without isActive (lines 552-561). Separate date-aware helpers already exist and are used only by the cost-sheet validator: getCurrentProcessorRate filters `effectiveTo: null` (validation service 125-142) and getRateAtDate does point-in-time (`effectiveFrom lte asOf` + `effectiveTo null OR gt asOf`, lines 170-187).
findings.planImpact: Any re-check should reuse getCurrentProcessorRate/getRateAtDate semantics (effectiveTo: null) rather than lookupRate's isActive-only filter, or the two mechanisms can disagree. Also: an as-of-date re-lookup is already possible via getRateAtDate — but note it takes a slabId, so it cannot answer "which slab now?" on its own.

findings.title: (c) PARTIAL: shrinkagePercent IS on the rate card and DOES drive required meters — but it is written uniformly across all slabs, so a pure quantity change does NOT change required meters
findings.evidence: schema backend/prisma/schema.prisma:2832; returned at processor-rate-v2.service.ts:960-961, :977; written across slabs at :640-666; quantity math backend/src/utils/greige-quantity.ts:43-85; consumers backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:1236, :1253, :4737, :4762 and backend/src/services/helpers/shrinkage-resolver.helper.ts:30-68
findings.detail: `shrinkagePercent Decimal? @db.Decimal(5,2)` is a column on processor_rate_card (schema:2832) — i.e. per (processor, processingType, printingType, greige, SLAB). lookupRate reads it with the comment "Shrinkage: ONLY from processor rate card (no fallback to greige master)" (lines 960-961). It reaches QUANTITY, not just cost: resolveShrinkagePercent (shrinkage-resolver.helper.ts:30-68, authority order rateCard → resolved card → greige master → 0) feeds calculateGreigeQuantity, which computes `need × (1 + wastage/100) ÷ (1 − shrinkage/100)` (greige-quantity.ts:5, 43-85) in MRP at mrp.service.ts:1236+1253 and 4737+4762. It ALSO enters cost separately as a greige uplift on the costing page (FabricCostingPage.tsx:1057-1060, 1082). CRITICAL CORRECTION to the memory-based premise: although the column is per-slab, the only write path sets it identically on every slab — saveProcessorRateMatrix does `updateMany({ where: {processorId, processingType, printingType}, data: { shrinkagePercent } })` with NO slabId filter (lines 644-666), and the type comments say "shrinkage is stored per greige, shared across slabs" (line 640, types file line 169). findRateCardsForShrinkage likewise ignores slabId (line 1719-1723) and returns `unambiguous: null` when a processor holds DIFFERENT values for one greige — which happens across DYEING vs print types, not across slabs. Side bug: that updateMany also has no isActive/effectiveTo filter, so it retroactively rewrites shrinkage on SUPERSEDED historical rate rows.
findings.planImpact: Downgrade the plan's "a quantity change at JWO changes REQUIRED METERS" claim: with the current data model, moving slabs changes ratePerMeter and screen amortization but NOT shrinkage, so required meters are unchanged. Required meters only change if the PROCESSOR or the DYEING/PRINTING/print-type changes. The re-check can therefore be a cost-only re-check at the JWO hop, unless the plan also intends to allow processor reassignment there.

findings.title: (d) CONFIRMED: model names are processor_rate_card (rates) and processor_quantity_slabs (slabs); slabs are keyed on processor+processingType only
findings.evidence: backend/prisma/schema.prisma:2796-2815 (processor_quantity_slabs), :2820-2871 (processor_rate_card); relation name "rate_card_slab" at :2810 and :2851
findings.detail: processor_quantity_slabs: id, processorId, processingType, slabOrder, minQuantity Decimal(10,2), maxQuantity Decimal(10,2), slabLabel, isActive, @@unique([processorId, processingType, slabOrder]) (lines 2796-2815). NOTE the slab table has NO printingType — slabs are shared across print types, as lookupRate's comment says (line 897). processor_rate_card: id, processorId, processingType, ratePerMeter Decimal(10,2), isActive, greigeId?, slabId?, printingType?, shrinkagePercent?, screenCostPerScreen?, screenType?, laceId?, effectiveFrom/effectiveTo/supersededById/previousRateValue/changeReasonCode/changeNotes, @@unique([processorId, processingType, printingType, greigeId, laceId, slabId, effectiveFrom]) named unique_rate_card_v4 (lines 2820-2871). Downstream FKs to it: fabric_width_cad.rateCardId (:4665-4666), order_bom_items.rateCardId (schema ~:245), style_costing_fabric_items and style_costing_lace_items (:2853-2854). Audit table is processor_rate_change_log (:2874+).
findings.planImpact: Use these exact names. Because slabs carry no printingType, a slab re-check needs only (processorId, processingType, quantity) to find the new slab, then (+greigeId, +printingType) to find the card.

findings.title: JWO creation never looks up a rate at all — agreedRatePerMeter is typed by hand and defaults to 0; only shrinkage is auto-filled from the rate card

findings.detail: The dyeing/printing Process-PO create endpoints take `agreedRatePerMeter` straight from req.body (dyeing:1396), validate only that it is present/non-negative (dyeing:1412-1413, schema backend/src/schemas/dyeing.schema.ts:156), and write it verbatim to job_work_orders (dyeing:1595). `totalAmount = qtyBillable × agreedRatePerMeter` where `qtyBillable = applyShrinkageLoss(qtySentMeters, resolvedExpectedShrinkage)` (dyeing:1562-1563). No processor_rate_card query occurs anywhere in that flow. On the frontend, `agreedRatePerMeter` is `useState<number>(0)` (ProcessPOCreateForm:94) bound to a manual input (lines 1090-1099) with an "isRateTbd" escape hatch; the ONE lookupRate call in that form (lines 302-307, passing `qtySentMeters || 1`) uses the result ONLY to set expectedShrinkage (lines 308-310) and DISCARDS rate.ratePerMeter. Backend fills only shrinkage via resolveJwoExpectedShrinkage (dyeing:1550-1554, helper shrinkage-resolver.helper.ts:82-93). job_work_orders has no rateCardId/slabId column at all (schema.prisma ~6812-6840), so a JWO carries zero traceability to the slab it was priced from.
findings.planImpact: The "re-check rate at JWO creation" step has nothing to compare against on the manual JWO path — there is no snapshot on the JWO and no lookup. The plan must either (i) auto-populate agreedRatePerMeter from lookupRate(qtySentMeters) and warn when it differs from the BOM's processingCost, and/or (ii) add rateCardId/slabId columns to job_work_orders for traceability. Note the frontend already has the lookup call wired at ProcessPOCreateForm:302 — the rate value just needs to be consumed.

findings.title: The existing rate re-check (validateCostSheetRates, blocking at ≥5%) PINS the original slabId, so it detects rate-value edits but is blind to quantity-driven slab changes
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/processor-rate-validation.service.ts:113-152 (slabId param), :277-283 and :329-335 (passes item.rateCard.slabId), :63-64 thresholds; invoked at backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:306-325 and backend/src/controllers/styleCosting.controller.ts:658
findings.detail: getCurrentProcessorRate takes `slabId?: string | null` and puts it in the where clause (lines 118, 131). validateCostSheetRates calls it with `item.rateCard?.slabId` (line 282 for fabric, line 334 for lace) — i.e. it asks "has the rate IN THE ORIGINALLY COSTED SLAB changed?", never "is the order quantity still in that slab?". It also passes no quantity at all. Order BOM creation blocks at ≥5% drift (order-bom.service.ts:306-325, BLOCKING_THRESHOLD_PERCENT=5 at validation:63) — so a guard already exists at the order hop, it is just measuring the wrong thing. Additional gap: `slabId: slabId || undefined` (line 131) means a null slabId silently drops the filter and matches ANY slab.
findings.planImpact: Do not add a parallel validator — extend this one. The minimal change is to pass the order's actual meters into validateCostSheetRates, re-run the slab match (lookupRate with the new quantity), and compare card-to-card rather than rate-to-rate within a pinned slab. Reusing the existing ≥5% BLOCKING / >0.01% WARNING thresholds keeps behaviour consistent.

findings.title: MRP does re-resolve a processing rate, but only as a fallback, and the resolver is blind to quantity, greige AND processing type
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/po-rate-resolver.service.ts:210-232; used at backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3102-3112 and :4995, :5026; price precedence at mrp.service.ts:3199-3208 and :3243-3252
findings.detail: resolveProcessingRate does `prisma.processor_rate_card.findFirst({ where: { processorId, isActive: true, ...(printingType ? {printingType} : {}) }, orderBy: {createdAt: 'desc'} })` (lines 213-221) — no greigeId, no processingType, no slabId, no quantity. It can return a DYEING card for a printing job or another greige's rate. However it is only a FALLBACK: the PO/JWO item price precedence is `manual override ?? snapshotPrice ?? costSheetRateMap ?? autoPriceMap ?? 0` (mrp.service.ts:3201-3208, 3245-3252), and snapshotPrice is `req.unitPrice` which for PROCESSING rows is the BOM's processingCost snapshot (mrp.service.ts:1722, 1759). So in the normal case the costing-time rate wins and the live resolver never fires — the claim "snapshotted once and never re-looked-up" holds in effect.
findings.planImpact: When the plan adds a JWO-time re-lookup, it must route through processor-rate-v2 lookupRate (greige + type + slab aware), NOT through po-rate-resolver.resolveProcessingRate, and should probably fix or narrow that resolver at the same time so the two paths cannot disagree.

findings.title: Confirmed divergence mechanics: BOM re-multiplies the cost sheet's per-piece consumption by the ORDER quantity while copying the costing-time processingCost verbatim; MRP then nets stock only on the GREIGE leg
findings.detail: generateBOM takes `orderQuantity = orderItem?.totalQuantity || order.totalQuantity` (order-bom.service.ts:502), recomputes `totalQuantity = quantityPerGarment × orderQuantity` (line 1066) and `totalWithWastage` (line 1068), but copies `processingCost: fabricItem.processingCost` and `rateCardId: fabricItem.rateCardId` unchanged from the cost sheet (lines 1108-1109; JSON fallback path lines 1177/1192/1222-1223). MRP then splits GREIGE_PROCESSED into two requirements: the GREIGE one carries availableStock/allocatedFromStock/shortfall (netting, lines 1698-1700) while the PROCESSING one hardcodes `availableStock: 0, allocatedFromStock: 0, shortfall: totalRequired` (lines 1739-1741) with `unitPrice: processingSnapshotPrice` from the BOM (lines 1722, 1759). So the exact three-hop divergence in the brief is real: costed meters (cadAverage × typed orderQuantityPcs) → BOM meters (cadAverage × real order qty) → JWO meters (post-netting), with ratePerMeter frozen at hop 1. Note the PROCESSING requirement is NOT stock-netted, so the 700m-after-netting case arises from the greige leg / manual JWO qtySentMeters, not from the PROCESSING requirement itself.
findings.planImpact: The order-confirmation re-check belongs at order-bom.service.ts:306 (where validateCostSheetRates already runs and where orderQuantity is known at line 502) — the quantity to re-look-up is `totalWithWastage` per fabric item, not the raw piece count. At the JWO hop the quantity is qtySentMeters (manual) or the requirement shortfall.

findings.title: Costing-time lookups can use a COMBINED batch-group quantity, so a naive per-JWO re-lookup would look like a rate increase and destroy the batch discount
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/FabricCostingPage.tsx:1138-1188 (batch quantity), :1190-1204 (individual comparison), :1219-1222 (batchRate/individualRate/batchSavings), :1277-1279; persisted key fabric_width_cad.processingBatchGroupColorId at backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4639; MRP consolidation at backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:1726-1727, :1763-1764, :1804-1809
findings.detail: When a row has `processingBatchGroupColorId`, the page sums cadMeters × qty across every row sharing greigeId + processorId + batch colour (deduped to newest per styleFabricId|width) and looks the rate up on that COMBINED quantity (lines 1142-1188), then applies the batch rate to all sibling rows (1227-1275) and reports savings vs the individual-quantity rate (1190-1209). MRP preserves the grouping when consolidating PROCESSING requirements (mrp.service.ts:1726-1727, 1763-1764, 1804-1809).
findings.planImpact: A re-check at JWO creation MUST compare against the same basis the costing used. If the costing priced 2500m as a batch of three colours and the JWO is one 700m colour, an individual-quantity re-lookup will always show a worse rate and would either false-alarm or, if auto-applied, silently discard the negotiated consolidation. The re-check needs to know whether the stored rate was a batch rate (today nothing persists that flag — batchRate/individualRate/batchSavings are frontend-only state, never saved in the payload at lines 1401-1440).

findings.title: Screen cost per meter is amortized over the costed quantity and is snapshotted too — a second quantity-sensitive number the plan does not mention
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/FabricCostingPage.tsx:1032, :1076-1079, :1082, :1425; schema backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4585 (screenCostPerMeter), :4583 (numberOfColors); source field processor_rate_card.screenCostPerScreen at :2833
findings.detail: `screenCostTotal = screenCostPerScreen × numberOfColors; screenCostPerMeter = screenCostTotal / totalQuantity` where `totalQuantity = row.cadMeters × (row.rowQuantity || orderQuantity)` (lines 1032, 1076-1079). It is added into totalCostPerMeter (line 1082) and saved as a flat `screenCostPerMeter` (line 1425 → fabric_width_cad.screenCostPerMeter, schema:4585). Screens are a FIXED cost per colour, so halving the quantity should double the per-meter screen charge — but the saved per-meter figure never changes. Transport in fixed-amount mode has the same shape (lines 1049-1053).
findings.planImpact: Any "re-check cost at order/JWO time" that only re-reads ratePerMeter will still be wrong for printed styles. Either re-derive screenCostPerMeter (and fixed-mode transport) from the new quantity, or persist screenCostPerScreen + numberOfColors + the costed quantity so downstream can. Only screenCostPerMeter (already amortized) is stored today.

findings.title: calculateFabricCost throws for any PRINTED fabric — lookupRate is called without the printingType it mandates

So every PRINTED fabric hitting POST /api/fabric-costing/calculate throws — uncaught in the single-fabric controller (fabric-costing.controller.ts:38-44 → 500), swallowed per-fabric in batch (controller lines 75-81 return `{error}`). Either fix it (thread printingType through FabricCostOptions, sourced from fabric_width_cad.rateCard.printingType which is already exposed at fabric-costing.controller.ts:703) or build the re-check on the lookupRate call directly.

It then maps SO items to order items, aggregating quantities per (colorId,sizeId) (388-425) and calls orderService.createWithItems (429). The two real insertion points are (1) saleOrder.service.ts:353-368, where the cost sheet is already fetched — ideal place to warn that SO qty ≠ costed qty; and (2) order-bom.service.ts:306, where processor rates are already validated and the true order quantity is known.

findings.title: A DRAFT order_bom survives item replacement with its stale orderQuantity, is orphaned (orderItemId SET NULL), and approve() never re-checks it against the order

After a PUT /orders/:id item replacement, DRAFT BOMs are neither blocked nor regenerated; the FK sets order_bom.orderItemId to NULL, so the BOM detaches from the (now deleted) order item but stays attached to orderId and stays DRAFT+isActive. approve() (2082) validates only bom.status==='DRAFT' and that the parent order is not CANCELLED — there is no comparison of order_bom_items.orderQuantity against the live order_items.totalQuantity. So a BOM costed at 2500 pcs can be approved for an order now carrying 1500 pcs, and its rates (unitPrice, greigeCost, processingCost, rateCardId) were slab-picked at the old quantity.

findings.title: order_item_costing (the cost snapshot + variance baseline) is CASCADE-deleted by the update path and is never recreated

findings.title: work_orders.orderItemId is SET NULL for every work order on item replacement; only PENDING ones are re-linked, so in-flight runs keep the old quantity and lose cost-variance tracking
findings.evidence: c:/Users/NEW/garment-erp/backend/prisma/migrations/20260804000000_baseline/migration.sql:10353 (work_orders.orderItemId ON DELETE SET NULL); c:/Users/NEW/garment-erp/backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:857-894 (sync scoped to status:'PENDING' only); c:/Users/NEW/garment-erp/backend/src/services/workOrder.service.ts:1237-1240 (updateActualCMTCosts silently returns when orderItemId is null)
findings.detail: The deleteMany at order.controller.ts:842 nulls work_orders.orderItemId for ALL work orders of the order, including IN_PRODUCTION / COMPLETED / DISPATCHED. The re-sync loop (857) queries only status:'PENDING', so any in-flight run is left with orderItemId=NULL and its ORIGINAL totalQuantity + work_order_breakup. workOrder.service.updateActualCMTCosts then logs 'has no order item, skipping' and returns (1237-1240), so actual CMT cost / costVarianceAmount / costVariancePercent are never recorded again for that run. The re-link also matches by styleId with findFirst (order.controller.ts:862-865), so two order items of the same style both bind to the first match.
findings.planImpact: Any amendment-propagation checkpoint has to decide the work-order policy explicitly (re-link + re-quantify, or refuse the edit outright when a non-PENDING work order exists). Silent SET NULL is not a safe default.

findings.title: PUT /api/orders/:id has no order-status gate and is not transactional
findings.evidence: c:/Users/NEW/garment-erp/backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:762-942 (no read of order.status anywhere); contrast c:/Users/NEW/garment-erp/backend/src/services/order.service.ts:418-461 updateOrder which DOES block CANCELLED but is never called by the controller; c:/Users/NEW/garment-erp/backend/src/utils/stateMachine.ts:36-43; c:/Users/NEW/garment-erp/backend/prisma/migrations/20260804000000_baseline/migration.sql:9582 (delivery_note_items.orderItemId ON DELETE SET NULL)
findings.detail: The controller never loads orders.status, so items and totalQuantity can be rewritten on an IN_PRODUCTION, COMPLETED, DISPATCHED or CANCELLED order (CANCELLED is a terminal state per stateMachine.ts:41). On a DISPATCHED order the delete also nulls delivery_note_items.orderItemId (baseline:9582), severing shipped lines from their order item. Separately, the whole path runs as loose top-level prisma calls — the dependency check (783-790), the two deleteMany calls (839-844), the per-item create loop (847-854), the work-order sync (857-894) and the final orders.update (906) are NOT wrapped in $transaction. A failure mid-loop leaves the order with zero/partial items and stale header totals; the check→delete window is also a TOCTOU race against a concurrent BOM approval or MRP run.
findings.planImpact: The checkpoint should be implemented inside a transaction that re-reads order.status and the dependency counts, not as a pre-check followed by unguarded writes.

findings.title: The order edit UI round-trips only order_items[0], so editing a multi-style production order created by startProduction silently deletes every other item

findings.title: No cumulative program quantity per processor+greige exists anywhere in the schema — a naive per-JWO slab lookup would systematically over-price split programs

findings.detail: `lookupRate` resolves the slab from ONE scalar `quantityMeters`. Economically this matters: costing quoted 2500 m at the 2000–5000 slab; if that program is dispatched as 4 JWOs of ~625 m, a per-JWO re-lookup drops every one of them into the 500–1000 slab and inflates the processing cost against a rate the processor never quoted. Minimum viable: persist `rateCardId` + `slabId` + `rateBasisQuantity` on job_work_orders (all three absent today), and define the lookup quantity as the requirement-chain program quantity (sum of `requirement_jwo_links.allocatedQuantity` across all live JWOs for the same requirement/order, plus the open remainder) rather than the single JWO's `qtySentMeters`. findings.title: Changing the processor at JWO time re-prices but never re-shrinks — the greige quantity stays computed from the ORIGINAL processor's card

A JWO-time rate re-check that resolves a new card for the actual processor MUST also surface that card's shrinkage and either (a) recompute `qtySentMeters`/`qtyBillable` before issue, or (b) hard-block the processor swap.
