The code comment at :3229-3230 documents a prior fix to the ADD-vs-REPLACE semantics, but the price is resolved in the first pass from `req.unitPrice` and is never revisited after the override lands. So an operator who types 700 into the wizard for a requirement costed at 2500 gets 700 m priced at the 2500 m slab rate, with no warning. `itemPrices` overrides exist (:3202, :3246) but are a separate, independent input the operator must remember to also change.
findings.planImpact: This is the cheapest, highest-signal place to put the plan's JWO-time re-check: a single hook after the second pass at mrp.service.ts:3236 that re-resolves the slab for each group's final quantity and either updates `unitPrice` or emits a blocking warning. It also means the plan should treat 'quantity was overridden' as an explicit trigger condition, not just 'quantity differs from costing'.

findings.title: A manual partial JWO closes the whole requirement — the uncovered balance is never re-offered, so the second JWO of a split program is never prompted
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/dyeing.controller.ts:1624-1643 and backend/src/controllers/printing.controller.ts:1593-1612 (status flipped to PO_GENERATED unconditionally; `allocatedQuantity` capped at `qtyBillable`; `shortfall` never reduced and no child requirement minted); contrast backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3498-3560 (MRP path DOES mint the remainder child); backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:4131-4154 (`updateJwoReceivedQuantity`: RECEIVED once `totalReceived >= totalAllocated`)
findings.detail: On the manual Process-PO path, a JWO covering 700 m of a 2500 m requirement flips that requirement to PO_GENERATED and creates one link allocated 700. When those 700 m come back, `totalReceived (700) >= totalAllocated (700)` and the requirement is marked RECEIVED (mrp.service.ts:4143-4144) — despite `shortfall` still saying 2500. The remaining 1800 m drops out of MRP entirely. The MRP-generated path handles this correctly via the MRP-12 split at :3501-3560; the two paths disagree.
findings.planImpact: Directly constrains the plan's cumulative-quantity design: on the manual path there is no durable record that the program is 2500 m, because the requirement is closed after the first partial. Any 'cumulative program quantity' basis must therefore either be sourced from `order_bom_items`/`material_requirements.totalRequired` (which survives) rather than open shortfall, or this manual-path split must be brought to parity with MRP-12 first.

findings.title: job_work_orders stores no rate provenance at all — the re-check has nothing to compare against and no place to record its answer
findings.evidence: backend/prisma/schema.prisma:6804-6964 (full job_work_orders model: `agreedRatePerMeter` at :6840, `isRateTbd` at :6841, `actualRate` at :6853 — no rateCardId, no slabId, no rateSource, no rateBasisQuantity); contrast :245/:280 (order_bom_items.rateCardId), :2046/:2058 (style_costing_fabric_items.rateCardId), :4665-4666 (fabric_width_cad.rateCardId); backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:2780-2804 (`buildJwoDataForProcessingPO` — the full JWO payload, no rate provenance fields)
findings.detail: Every upstream costing artefact records WHICH rate card it used. The JWO — the document the processor is actually paid against — records only a bare number. There is consequently no way to answer 'which slab was this job billed at', no way to detect after the fact that a JWO was priced off a different tier than its quantity implies, and no field for a re-check to write its result into.
findings.planImpact: A schema migration adding `rateCardId`, `slabId`, `rateSource`, and `rateBasisQuantity` to job_work_orders is a prerequisite for the plan's JWO-time re-check to be auditable rather than advisory. The same three fields also let a backfill script classify existing JWOs as correctly- or incorrectly-slabbed, which the plan will need to size the historical exposure.

findings.title: The generic JWO create endpoint skips the shrinkage resolver that the dyeing/printing paths use
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/job-work-order.controller.ts:196-201 (`expectedShrinkage = isFabricProcess ? (body.expectedShrinkage ?? null) : null`; `qtyBillable` derived from it), :232 (`agreedRatePerMeter: isKaaj ? 0 : body.agreedRate`); contrast backend/src/controllers/dyeing.controller.ts:1550-1554 and backend/src/controllers/printing.controller.ts:1520 (both call `resolveJwoExpectedShrinkage`); backend/src/services/helpers/shrinkage-resolver.helper.ts:70-93 (the helper exists precisely to stop a null expectedShrinkage printing 'return 100%' on the challan)
findings.detail: `resolveJwoExpectedShrinkage` was written (per its own docstring at :71-80) because the dyeing/printing endpoints took `expectedShrinkage` straight from the body and a caller that omitted it produced a challan demanding 100% return. The generic create surface at job-work-order.controller.ts:196-201 still has exactly that behaviour — it never calls the helper. Its only two consumers are the two controllers listed above.
findings.planImpact: Small, but it is on the plan's critical path: if the plan adds a rate re-check at JWO creation it will touch this handler anyway, and resolving the rate card there makes the card's `shrinkagePercent` available in the same breath. Wiring `resolveJwoExpectedShrinkage` in at the same time closes the gap for free.

findings.title: Greige rate is snapshotted at costing and NEVER re-looked-up at order confirmation, MRP recalc, PO creation, or JWO — same defect class as processor rates
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:1681-1685, 1715-1717; backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:1956-1958 (recalc re-copies same snapshot); backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3200-3208 and 3244-3252 (price precedence); backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:1107; backend/src/controllers/styleCosting.controller.ts:382
findings.detail: Full chain is a pure copy with no re-derivation: fabric_width_cad.greigeCostPerMeter -> style_costing_fabric_items.greigeCost (styleCosting.controller.ts:382 `greigeCost: cad.greigeCostPerMeter ?? null`) -> order_bom_items.greigeCost (order-bom.service.ts:1107) -> material_requirements.unitPrice with rateSource='ORDER_BOM' (mrp.service.ts:1715-1716) -> purchase_order_items.unitPrice. At PO generation the precedence is `itemPrices[key] ?? itemPrices[materialId] ?? snapshotPrice ?? costSheetRateMap ?? autoPriceMap ?? 0` (mrp.service.ts:3201-3208), so the BOM snapshot ALWAYS wins over the live resolver whenever it is non-null — the live resolver is only reachable for legacy/manual rows with a null snapshot. MRP recalculation (mrp.service.ts:1936-1959) explicitly re-writes unitPrice from the same BOM snapshot, so quantity changes never re-price. There is no code path anywhere that re-reads the greige rate at order confirmation or JWO creation.
findings.planImpact: The plan's 'add rate re-checks at order confirmation and JWO creation' must cover the GREIGE leg too, not only processor rates. The single highest-leverage insertion point is mrp.service.ts:1681-1685 (calculation) plus the price precedence at 3201-3208/3244-3252 — a re-check must either overwrite req.unitPrice or be inserted ABOVE snapshotPrice in the precedence chain, otherwise it will be silently ignored.

findings.title: Greige PO from MRP shortfall is priced ONLY from the costed snapshot; there is no last-PO, no stock-WAC and effectively no supplier-master fallback
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/po-rate-resolver.service.ts:172-208 (resolveGreigeRate); backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3075-3079 (autoPriceMap), 3115-3132; backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3269-3273 (zero-price throw); backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:103-119, 158-174 (material_suppliers auto-created with NO supplierPrice)
findings.detail: resolveGreigeRate has exactly two sources: (1) style_costing_fabric_items.greigeCost for the cost sheet (po-rate-resolver.service.ts:178-194) and (2) material_suppliers.supplierPrice (196-205). It never consults greige_stock, greige_master.costPerMeter, greige_master.lastPurchaseRate, or the last greige PO/GRN. Its supplier fallback is nearly always empty because MRP auto-creates material_suppliers rows with only supplierId/isPreferred and no supplierPrice (mrp.service.ts:103-111, 158-166, and the same pattern at 213/268/323/378/433/488/566/620); material_suppliers.supplierPrice is only ever written from the Material Master UI (material.service.ts:176, 418). Net effect: the greige PO rate = the number typed on the CAD row weeks earlier, or the PO generation throws 'Cannot generate PO with zero-price items' (mrp.service.ts:3270-3273).
findings.planImpact: Any 'else use costed rate' branch in the plan is today the ONLY branch. Adding a stock-WAC / last-purchase source requires new code in resolveGreigeRate (po-rate-resolver.service.ts:172) — the data exists (greige_stock.purchaseCost, greige_master.lastPurchaseRate) but nothing reads it.

findings.title: LANDED_PRICE costing rows produce a GREIGE BOM line with greigeCost=null, so MRP prices the greige PO at the ALL-IN fabric rate
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/FabricCostingPage.tsx:1411 and 1414 and 1420; backend/src/controllers/styleCosting.controller.ts:368; backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:1076, 1082, 1107-1108; backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:1681-1685
findings.detail: In LANDED_PRICE mode the save payload sets `greigeCostPerMeter: null` and `processingCostPerMeter: null` but still sends `processorId: row.processorId` (FabricCostingPage.tsx:1411, 1414, 1420). The cost sheet then derives sourcingStrategy purely from the processor: `sourcingStrategy: cad.processorId ? 'GREIGE_PROCESSED' : 'READY_FABRIC'` (styleCosting.controller.ts:368). order-bom.service.ts:1082 therefore emits materialType='GREIGE' with greigeCost=null and unitPrice = the all-in landed ₹/m (line 1076). MRP's fallback at mrp.service.ts:1681-1685 (`bomItem.greigeCost ? ... : bomItem.unitPrice`) then prices the GREIGE requirement — and the resulting greige PO to the weaver — at the full landed price (greige + shrinkage + processing + transport), overstating greige spend by roughly the processing margin. The linked PROCESSING requirement simultaneously gets unitPrice=null (line 1722) and falls through to the naive live resolver.
findings.planImpact: A rate re-check at order confirmation would mask but not fix this: the correct fix is either to clear processorId in LANDED_PRICE mode or to refuse the unitPrice fallback at mrp.service.ts:1681-1685 for GREIGE. Plan should add an explicit guard rather than letting the all-in rate flow into a greige PO.

findings.title: Three different greige-rate resolvers with three different priority orders disagree on the same greige
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:399-438; backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:599-634 (and duplicate at 720-754); backend/src/controllers/cad-planning.controller.ts:3530-3563
findings.detail: (a) fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:421-438 — latest fabric_procurement.ratePerUnit -> getGreigeWAC (stock_settings.valuationRate) -> greige_master.costPerMeter; emits in-memory sources 'PROCUREMENT' | 'STOCK_WAC' | 'GREIGE_MASTER'. (b) fabric-costing.controller.ts:616-634 — MOST RECENT of (latest procurement.purchaseDate, latest greige_stock.receivedDate) then greige_master.costPerMeter; emits 'GREIGE_PROCUREMENT' | 'GREIGE_STOCK' | 'GREIGE_MASTER'. (c) cad-planning.controller.ts:3555-3563 (CAD auto-costing seed) — latest procurement -> greige_master.costPerMeter ONLY, stock is never consulted; emits the persisted enum PROCUREMENT | GREIGE_MASTER. Resolver (a) backs CostSheetForm/SourcingStrategySelector; (b) backs FabricCostingPage; (c) is what actually gets written to fabric_width_cad. The same greige can show three different rates on three screens.
findings.planImpact: A re-check must pick ONE authority. Reusing any of the three as-is perpetuates the disagreement; the plan should name the canonical resolver (and note that (a) and (b) use different, non-equivalent definitions of 'latest').

findings.title: greigeRateSource on fabric_width_cad is stale/dead metadata — Fabric Costing saves the rate without ever updating the source columns
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:1109-1137 (update path) and 1019-1072 (clone path); backend/src/controllers/cad-planning.controller.ts:3567-3578 (only writer); backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4630-4633
findings.detail: cad-planning.controller.ts:3567-3578 is the ONLY writer of greigeRateSource / greigeRateSourceDate / greigeRateManualOverride / greigeRateOverrideReason, and it runs only on the auto-costing seed, only when `updatedCad.totalCostPerMeter === null` (cad-planning.controller.ts:3515-3519). saveFabricCosting writes greigeCostPerMeter (fabric-costing.controller.ts:1119) but does NOT touch any of the four source columns; the CLONE branch (1047) copies the rate but leaves the source columns null on the new row. So after any real costing save the persisted greigeRateSource describes the ORIGINAL auto-seed, not the committed number. Enum values STOCK_VALUATION and MANUAL_OVERRIDE (schema.prisma:9196-9201) are never written by any code; greigeRateManualOverride/greigeRateOverrideReason are only ever set to null (cad-planning.controller.ts:3573-3574). GreigeRateSourceEnum in backend/src/schemas/cadPlanning.schema.ts:25 is exported but referenced by no request schema.
findings.planImpact: Do NOT use fabric_width_cad.greigeRateSource as the input to a staleness/re-check decision — it is unreliable. Either the re-check must write it (making it truthful) or it must be ignored entirely. The frontend already sidesteps it: frontend/src/utils/greigeRate.ts resolves 'COMMITTED' vs live purely from greigeCostPerMeterSaved vs the live API value.

findings.title: PARTIAL: weighted-average cost data exists on greige_stock but is per-lot and never re-blended; the shared helper is unused for greige
findings.evidence: backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4340-4341; backend/src/services/greige-stock.service.ts:197-198; backend/src/utils/currency.ts:210-228; backend/src/services/WeightedAverageCostService.ts:53
findings.detail: greige_stock has purchaseCost + weightedAvgCost (schema.prisma:4340-4341), but createGreigeStock sets BOTH to the same incoming rate at creation (greige-stock.service.ts:197-198) and nothing ever recomputes weightedAvgCost afterwards — the only other greige_stock.weightedAvgCost reference in the codebase is a read. The unique key (schema.prisma:4397: greigeId+procurementId+greigeWidth+qualityGrade+supplierId+processorId+sourceChallanId) guarantees one row per receipt, so 'weightedAvgCost' is a per-lot duplicate of purchaseCost, not a rolling average. calculateWeightedAverageCost (currency.ts:210-228) and WeightedAverageCostService.calculateWeightedAverageCost (WeightedAverageCostService.ts:53) exist but are called ONLY from their own unit tests (backend/src/__tests__/unit/currency.test.ts:223, backend/src/services/__tests__/WeightedAverageCostService.test.ts) — no production greige callsite. Reads that need a single rate hand-roll it: greige-stock.service.ts:425 (`weightedAvgCost || purchaseCost || 0`), fabric-costing.controller.ts:543-558.
findings.planImpact: 'Use stock weighted-avg cost when issuing from stock' is IMPLEMENTABLE — per-lot purchaseCost is reliably populated — but the plan must compute the blend at read time (qty-weighted across AVAILABLE lots) rather than assuming greige_stock.weightedAvgCost is a real WAC. It is not.

findings.title: getGreigeWAC (the STOCK_WAC branch) reads stock_settings.valuationRate, which the greige GRN path never populates — the branch is dead for PO-received greige
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/helpers/derived-stock.helper.ts:134-148; backend/src/services/grn.service.ts:1523-1554; backend/src/services/helpers/material-sync.helper.ts:115-121, 155-161; backend/src/services/stockLevel.service.ts:263-336; backend/src/services/stockMovement.service.ts:99-168, 284
findings.detail: getGreigeWAC requires `stock_settings.valuationRate IS NOT NULL` (derived-stock.helper.ts:136-143). valuationRate is written in only two places: stockLevel.service.increaseStock (263-336) — which no production code calls, only tests — and stockMovement.service.increaseStockInTx (99-168), reachable only from createStockIn/createBulkStockIn (284, 385). The PO->GRN greige receipt path calls greigeStockService.createGreigeStock then `syncStockLevelQuantity(greige.id, actualQty, warehouseId, undefined, tx)` (grn.service.ts:1523-1554), and syncStockLevelQuantity takes no rate parameter at all and only increments/decrements quantity (material-sync.helper.ts:115-121, 155-161). So greige bought against a PO never gets a valuationRate, getGreigeWAC returns null, and fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:430-433 can never reach 'STOCK_WAC' for it. Separately, getGreigeWAC is not a weighted average at all: `ORDER BY ss."valuationRate" ASC LIMIT 1` (derived-stock.helper.ts:142-143) picks the CHEAPEST warehouse's rate.
findings.planImpact: Do not build the plan's stock-WAC branch on getGreigeWAC/stock_settings — it is empty for the main receipt path and returns a min, not an average. Source the blend from greige_stock lots (purchaseCost x quantityAvailable) instead.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: greige issuance to a JWO DOES record the cost of the issued greige — in three places, but only one of them exists for single-lot issues
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/greige-stock.service.ts:569-591 (greige_stock_transaction.costPerUnit/totalValue); backend/src/services/job-work-issuance.service.ts:470-495 (components, gated on lots.length>1), 553-575 (jwo.declaredValue); backend/src/services/grn.service.ts:2902-2924 (consumed at receipt)
findings.detail: (1) Every consume writes greige_stock_transaction.costPerUnit = purchaseCost ?? weightedAvgCost and totalValue (greige-stock.service.ts:569-591). (2) job_work_order_components.rate / rateAtIssue / declaredValue are written from the same lot cost (job-work-issuance.service.ts:473-489) BUT the whole block is inside `if (lots.length > 1)` (line 470) — a single-lot issue creates no component row and therefore no rateAtIssue snapshot. (3) job_work_orders.declaredValue is stamped for all lots (553-575). This data is actually consumed: at JWO receipt grn.service.ts:2902-2924 computes weightedGreigeCost from the components (falling back to greigeStockLot.purchaseCost for single-lot) and sets the resulting fabric_stock.weightedAvgCost = processingRate + sourceCost (2920-2924, 2952-2953).
findings.planImpact: The plan's premise that issued-greige cost is unrecorded is REFUTED — it is recorded. What is missing is any comparison back to the costed rate: nothing reconciles greige_stock_transaction.costPerUnit / declaredValue against order_bom_items.greigeCost. A variance surface, not new capture, is what's needed. Also note the single-lot gap at job-work-issuance.service.ts:470 if the plan intends to read rateAtIssue uniformly.

findings.title: BOM width change refreshes unitPrice from the new CAD but copies greigeCost/processingCost from the OLD item
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:1719 vs 1738-1740
findings.detail: In the width-change BOM revision, `unitPrice = cad.totalCostPerMeter ? Number(cad.totalCostPerMeter) : Number(item.unitPrice)` is taken from the NEW CAD row (order-bom.service.ts:1719), while greigeCost, processingCost and rateCardId are copied verbatim from the old item (1738-1740). Since MRP prices greige POs off greigeCost (mrp.service.ts:1681) and processing off processingCost (1722), a width change moves the all-in BOM value to the new CAD's numbers but leaves the actual procurement rates — and the rate card that pins process/print type and shrinkage — pointing at the superseded width. fabricWidthInches and selectedCadId ARE updated (1755-1756), so the row becomes internally inconsistent.
findings.planImpact: A re-check at order confirmation would repair this incidentally, but only if it re-derives greigeCost/processingCost/rateCardId from selectedCadId rather than trusting the BOM row. Worth an explicit step in the plan.

findings.title: Order-confirmation CAD clone drops processorId, rateCardId, orderQuantityPcs, shrinkage and costingStyleId while copying the greige rate
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:677-715 (esp. 697-700); contrast backend/src/controllers/cad-approval.controller.ts:445-459
findings.detail: When an order is confirmed, COSTING CAD rows are cloned to RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION (order.controller.ts:677-715). The create copies greigeCostPerMeter, processingPricePerMeter, totalCostPerMeter and costInputMode (697-700) but omits processorId, rateCardId, orderQuantityPcs, shrinkagePercent, shrinkageCostPerMeter, transportCostPerMeter, screenCostPerMeter and costingStyleId. The parallel 'copy as draft' path in cad-approval.controller.ts:445-459 copies all of those. orderQuantityPcs is the quantity that drove the processor rate-slab lookup, so the clone loses the evidence of which slab the price came from at exactly the hop where the plan wants to re-check.
findings.planImpact: A re-check at order confirmation must read the slab quantity from the ORDER (order_items quantity), not from the cloned CAD row — orderQuantityPcs will be null there. Alternatively fix the clone to carry processorId/rateCardId/orderQuantityPcs first, or the re-check will have nothing to compare against.

findings.title: greige_master.lastPurchaseRate is maintained on every GRN but read by nothing
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/helpers/greige-rate.helper.ts:27-44; backend/src/services/grn.service.ts:1558-1563; backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4288-4291
findings.detail: updateGreigeLastPurchaseRate writes greige_master.lastPurchaseRate/lastPurchaseAt on each greige receipt (greige-rate.helper.ts:35-41, called from grn.service.ts:1558). A repo-wide grep for `lastPurchaseRate` across backend/src and frontend/src returns only the writer and its own doc comment — no reader. The schema comment at 4288-4289 calls it 'Informational: the costing page already reads the live procurement row directly'. Meanwhile greige_master.costPerMeter is a hand-set planning rate deliberately not auto-updated (schema.prisma:4284-4287, greige-rate.helper.ts:4-8) and is the LAST fallback in two of the three resolvers.
findings.planImpact: lastPurchaseRate is the cleanest ready-made 'live greige rate' signal for a re-check comparison — already maintained, already guarded against zero-rate GRNs, and free of the master-rate self-reinforcing loop the helper's comment warns about. The plan should prefer it over re-querying fabric_procurement.

findings.title: 'ORDER_BOM' rate source is rendered as silent/trusted in the PO wizard, so a stale costed greige rate reaches the user with zero visual warning
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/BulkPOGenerationDialog.tsx:653-654, 693-704; backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:5130-5137
findings.detail: The PO preview computes effectiveRateSource (mrp.service.ts:5131-5137) and the dialog shows an amber warning badge only when `item.rateSource && item.rateSource !== 'ORDER_BOM'` (BulkPOGenerationDialog.tsx:653-654) — the comment reads 'Exception-only badge — show ONLY when rateSource is NOT ORDER_BOM (silence = trusted)'. Since every greige requirement generated from a BOM carries rateSource='ORDER_BOM' (mrp.service.ts:1716), the exact case the plan is trying to catch — a months-old costed rate applied to a quantity that has since collapsed from 2500m to 700m — is the one case the UI stays silent about.
findings.planImpact: If the plan adds a backend re-check, the UI must be inverted for the stale case: either introduce a new rateSource value (e.g. 'ORDER_BOM_STALE') or ship the live rate alongside so the dialog can flag divergence. Simply fixing the backend leaves the wizard reassuringly quiet.

findings.title: MRP nets greige stock across ALL widths, so an allocation can be satisfied by lots the JWO cannot physically use
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:1277-1303; contrast 1306-1318 (fabric path filters cutableWidth ±0.5)
findings.detail: The GREIGE stock aggregate filters on greigeId/status/quantityAvailable/processorId only (mrp.service.ts:1278-1289) — no greigeWidth predicate — while the FABRIC branch immediately below filters `cutableWidth: { gte: bomWidth - 0.5, lte: bomWidth + 0.5 }` (1310-1314). convertToGreigeProcessing has the same width-blind aggregate (4776-4780). Downstream the JWO does care about width: it derives askedFinishedWidthInches from the BOM width and validates against greige_master.greigeWidth (mrp.service.ts:3363-3379), and stamps greigeWidthInches from the actual issued lot (job-work-issuance.service.ts:572-574).
findings.planImpact: Because netting is width-blind, the 'stock' portion of a greige requirement may be valued (and later issued) from a lot of the wrong width at a different purchaseCost than the plan assumes. Any 'use stock WAC when issuing from stock' rule must decide whether to blend across all widths (matching today's netting) or only matching widths (matching physical reality) — the two give different rates.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: editing a price-approved costing row is HARD-BLOCKED (400), never a silent un-approve — the plan's "force re-cost on the Fabric Costing page" is unreachable without an explicit unapprove
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:1094-1104; backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:939-966; backend/src/__tests__/integration/fabric-costing-approval.test.ts:174-205; frontend/src/pages/FabricCostingPage.tsx:1352-1389
findings.detail: saveFabricCosting refetches the target row and throws `ValidationError('Cannot change the costing for an approved option (...). Unapprove it first.')` when costingApprovalStatus is APPROVED **or** ALTERNATE_APPROVED (fabric-costing.controller.ts:1097-1104). It does NOT silently un-approve, and it does NOT partially save: the throw is inside the `Promise.all(fabricCostings.map(...))` at :1005, and there is no surrounding transaction, so a mixed batch can half-write other rows before the rejected row's promise rejects. Client-sent costingApprovalStatus/costingApprovedBy/costingApprovedAt are rejected with 403 ForbiddenError (:939-966), so the approval columns are genuinely single-writer (approve/unapprove/promote/reject only). The frontend never even reaches the 400: handleSave filters approved rows out of the payload (`approvedRows` at :1356-1360, `rowsToSave` at :1361) and shows `notify.info('N approved costing(s) unchanged. Unapprove on the Options page first to modify.')` (:1385-1389). Net: a user told to "re-cost at order quantity" on an APPROVED row gets a silent no-op, not an edit. Test pins this contract (fabric-costing-approval.test.ts:174-192 expects 400 + price unchanged at 52).
findings.planImpact: The plan's remediation step ('block at order confirmation and send the user to re-cost on the Fabric Costing page') has no working target. Any fix must either (a) route through unapprove→edit→re-approve — which findings 2/3/4 show is itself broken — or (b) abandon mutating the style-level row and store the order-adjusted rate in an order-scoped table (see finding 10).

findings.title: CONFIRMED: the 6-column unique index makes 'unapprove → clone at order qty → re-approve' structurally impossible — a per-quantity variant can NEVER be CAD-approved while order 1's row is APPROVED
findings.evidence: backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4682; backend/prisma/migrations/20260804000000_baseline/migration.sql:7914; backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:1009-1073 (clone copies every tuple column); backend/src/controllers/cad-approval.controller.ts:129-141; backend/src/services/style.service.ts:2474-2483
findings.detail: The live unique index is `(costingStyleId, componentName, style_fabric_id, cutableWidth, purpose, approval_status)` — it contains NO quantity column. The quantity-change clone path (fabric-costing.controller.ts:1009-1073) copies cutableWidth (:1023), componentName (:1029), styleFabricId (:1030) and purpose (:1043) verbatim from the source and sets costingStyleId = the same styleId (:1041), so the clone differs from order 1's row in exactly ONE indexed column: approvalStatus, which it sets to null (:1067). The CREATE succeeds only because Postgres treats NULLs as distinct. The moment anyone CAD-approves that clone — `approvalStatus: 'APPROVED'` at cad-approval.controller.ts:137, or the bulk flip at style.service.ts:2474-2483 — the tuple collides with order 1's still-APPROVED row and Postgres raises a unique violation. Neither cad-approval.controller.ts nor cad-planning.controller.ts contains any P2002 handler (grep: zero matches), so the user gets a raw Prisma 500, not a business error. The only way to free the slot is to CAD-reject order 1's row, which also wipes its price approval (finding 6).
findings.planImpact: Kills the 'unapprove → re-cost → re-approve' remediation outright: even after re-pricing, the order-2 variant cannot be made CAD-approved, and CAD approval is a hard requirement of both the order-confirmation clone gate and the cost-sheet gate. Either the index must gain orderQuantityPcs (a schema migration touching a live constraint, plus the partial index at migration 20260822092844:50-52), or the order-adjusted rate must live outside fabric_width_cad.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: a re-costed clone is invisible to the order-confirmation gate — the in-flight order still clones the STALE style-level costing
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:635-658; backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:1066-1071; backend/src/controllers/style-costing-calc.controller.ts:89-108
findings.detail: updateOrderStatus's RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION auto-clone selects `purpose: 'COSTING'` AND `approvalStatus: 'APPROVED'` AND `costingApprovalStatus: { in: ['APPROVED','ALTERNATE_APPROVED'] }` AND `totalCostPerMeter: { not: null }` (order.controller.ts:637-640). A clone born from the quantity-change path has `approvalStatus: null` and `costingApprovalStatus: null` (fabric-costing.controller.ts:1067-1068), so it fails BOTH halves of the gate. Meanwhile order 1's original row still satisfies the gate. Result: the user 're-costs at order quantity', hits Confirm, and the RM CAD rows are cloned from the OLD 2500-pc costing anyway — the exact bug the plan set out to fix, now with a false sense of remediation. The same asymmetry exists on the cost-sheet gate (style-costing-calc.controller.ts:89-108, both paths require approvalStatus APPROVED + costingApprovalStatus APPROVED/ALTERNATE_APPROVED).
findings.planImpact: Any gate added at order confirmation must read the rate the order will actually be costed at, not the rate the user typed on a new unapproved row. Confirms the plan needs an order-scoped write that the confirmation gate itself consumes.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: approving a per-quantity variant demotes order 1's row to ALTERNATE_APPROVED, which STILL passes every downstream gate — both quantity variants then clone, double-counting fabric
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:1426-1487; backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:639; backend/src/controllers/style-costing-calc.controller.ts:94,105; backend/src/__tests__/integration/fabric-costing-approval.test.ts:115-137
findings.detail: approveCostingOption's first updateMany demotes every costed sibling matching (costingStyleId, componentName, fabricId, greigeId, styleFabricId, patternPartId, purpose) to `costingApprovalStatus: 'ALTERNATE_APPROVED'`, `isPreferred: false`, keeping costingApprovedBy/At (fabric-costing.controller.ts:1430-1448). That is exactly the tuple order 1's row shares with the order-2 variant. So approving the order-2 price silently strips order 1's row of PRIMARY status — corrupting order 1's recorded basis with no audit trail beyond the status flip. Worse, ALTERNATE_APPROVED is accepted by the order-confirmation clone (`in: ['APPROVED','ALTERNATE_APPROVED']`, order.controller.ts:639) and by both cost-sheet gates (style-costing-calc.controller.ts:94 and :105). So if both variants ever reach CAD approval, order confirmation clones BOTH into RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION for the same component/width — duplicated RM rows and double-counted fabric requirement. Only the PARTIAL index (`WHERE costing_approval_status = 'APPROVED'`, migration 20260822092844:50-52) constrains the primary; it does not constrain ALTERNATE_APPROVED at all.
findings.planImpact: Confirms suspicion (a) concretely: mutating/re-approving at order-2 quantity corrupts order 1's basis. Also means an order-scoped fix must NOT create a second APPROVED-family row on the same tuple, or the RM clone double-counts.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: cost-sheet generation picks CAD rows by updatedAt desc with NO approval filter — a fresh, unapproved order-2 clone silently becomes the style's cost basis for every order
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/style-costing-calc.controller.ts:142-154, 183-193; backend/src/controllers/style-costing-calc.controller.ts:158-176
findings.detail: After the gate passes, the preview query is `costingStyleId: styleId, purpose: 'COSTING', totalCostPerMeter: { not: null }` ordered `updatedAt: desc` (:142-154) — no costingApprovalStatus filter, no approvalStatus filter, no order scoping. It then takes the FIRST row per componentName (`processedComponents` de-dup at :183-193, comment 'we have latest first'). So the instant a user saves a re-costed clone at order-2 quantity, that clone becomes the newest row for the component and drives the next cost-sheet generation for the STYLE — for every buyer, every order. (Only the RM fallback at :158-172 filters on costingApprovalStatus: 'APPROVED'.)
findings.planImpact: Even if the plan avoided approval entirely and just 'saved a re-cost', it would contaminate the style-level cost sheet cross-order. Strengthens the case for an order-scoped storage location that the cost-sheet path never reads.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: the unapprove→edit→re-approve window breaks every OTHER order's flow, and also unlocks CAD geometry edits that would invalidate the approved basis
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:1537-1545; backend/src/controllers/cad-planning.utils.ts:223-231; backend/src/controllers/style-costing-calc.controller.ts:120-129; backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:660-669; backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:1838-1840
findings.detail: unapproveCostingOption nulls costingApprovalStatus/By/At and isPreferred on the shared style-level row (fabric-costing.controller.ts:1537-1545). During that window: (1) generating/regenerating a cost sheet for the style throws 'Cost sheet needs a fabric row that is BOTH CAD-approved ... and costing-approved with a price' (style-costing-calc.controller.ts:120-129) — for ALL orders of the style; (2) any other order confirmed in that window gets `skipped: true, reason: 'No fully-approved COSTING CAD found...'` and produces ZERO RM CAD rows (order.controller.ts:660-669) — and because the per-item failure is swallowed (:728-741) the order still flips to IN_PRODUCTION with no RM basis; (3) promoteCostingOption refuses (:1838-1840); (4) validateCADModification's price-approval lock at cad-planning.utils.ts:226-231 stops applying, so CAD Planning can edit cutableWidth/cadMeters or delete the row (cascading cad_size_breakdown) while the price is unapproved — silently invalidating the geometry order 1 was priced on.
findings.planImpact: The window is not a benign transaction; it is a style-wide outage plus a temporary removal of the CAD edit lock. Any plan that requires unapprove/re-approve on the shared row must at minimum be transactional and must re-assert the CAD lock — which the current endpoints cannot do (unapprove and approve are separate HTTP calls with a human in between).

findings.title: CONFIRMED: freeing the unique-index slot requires a CAD rejection, and BOTH rejection paths wipe price approvals — the style-level one wipes every row of the style
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/cad-approval.controller.ts:244-261; backend/src/services/style.service.ts:2526-2541; backend/src/__tests__/integration/fabric-costing-approval.test.ts:265-296; CLAUDE.md:138
findings.detail: Row-level rejectCADPurpose sets approvalStatus REJECTED and simultaneously nulls costingApprovalStatus/costingApprovedBy/costingApprovedAt and isPreferred (cad-approval.controller.ts:247-260). Style-level rejectCADPlan does the same via a single updateMany over EVERY fabric_width_cad row linked to ANY style_fabric of the style (style.service.ts:2527-2541) — one click destroys the approved basis of every order ever costed on that style. Cost numbers survive; approvals do not (pinned by fabric-costing-approval.test.ts:291-296). This is the documented policy (CLAUDE.md:138).
findings.planImpact: There is no non-destructive path to re-slot a per-quantity CAD variant. Confirms suspicion (b) at the CAD half of the split as well: the approval machinery blocks the plan from both directions.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: order confirmation cannot BLOCK where the plan assumes — the status commits before the check point, and the RM loop swallows all errors
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:589, 599, 604-605, 728-741, 745-755; backend/src/services/saleOrder.service.ts:350-368
findings.detail: updateOrderStatus calls `orderService.updateStatus(...)` at :589 — the DB status flip to IN_PRODUCTION is already committed — and only then enters the `if (status === 'IN_PRODUCTION' ...)` block at :599. Inside, every per-item body is wrapped in try/catch (:605, :728-741) marked `// allow-swallow`, which records `skipped: true, reason: 'Error during cloning: ...'` into the response payload and continues; the endpoint still returns 200 with 'Order status updated successfully' (:745-755). A rate-slab check added inside that loop therefore cannot block anything. The other confirmation door, saleOrderService.startProduction, gates only on a style-level APPROVED style_costing for purpose RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION/PRODUCTION (saleOrder.service.ts:353-368) — style-scoped, quantity-blind, shared by every order of the style.
findings.planImpact: The block must be inserted BEFORE order.controller.ts:589 (pre-transition validation) and/or in orderService.updateStatus, and must throw outside the swallow. Any 'block' written into the RM clone loop is a no-op.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: no quantity-slab re-lookup exists anywhere downstream; the only 'live' processing-rate resolver ignores quantity, greige and the pinned rateCardId entirely
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/processor-rate-v2.service.ts:877; backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:837; backend/src/services/fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:501; backend/src/services/po-rate-resolver.service.ts:210-231; backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:3101-3112, 3346-3350; backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:2796
findings.detail: `lookupRate` (the slab-aware resolver, processor-rate-v2.service.ts:877) has exactly two callers, both at costing time: fabric-costing.controller.ts:837 (POST /lookup-rate) and fabric-cost-calculation.service.ts:501. Downstream, MRP/PO/JWO use `resolveProcessingRate` (po-rate-resolver.service.ts:210-231), which queries `processor_rate_card` by processorId + isActive (+ printingType when known), `orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }`, `take` first — it never filters by slabId, greigeId, quantity, or the BOM line's pinned rateCardId. Its fallback is the snapshotted `req.processingCost` (mrp.service.ts:3112, 5006-5013). The JWO's agreedRatePerMeter is then the value-weighted average of those PO item unitPrices over billable meters (mrp.service.ts:3346-3350 → buildJwoDataForProcessingPO :2796). So at JWO time the rate is either an arbitrary newest card or the costing-time snapshot — never the correct slab for the JWO quantity.
findings.planImpact: The 're-check at JWO creation' half of the plan has no existing slab-aware call site to reuse downstream; it must call processor-rate-v2 `lookupRate` with the netted quantity. Also flags a second, independent defect: resolveProcessingRate should honour orderBomItem.rateCardId / the slab, or it will keep quoting the wrong card even after the fix.

findings.title: Storage-location analysis: order_bom_items is the only order-scoped, single-writer-clean home; the RM CAD clone and order_item_costing are both dead ends
findings.evidence: backend/prisma/schema.prisma:161-191, 206-213, 240-247, 285-289; backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:1106-1109, 1213-1235, 1558-1561, 1737-1740, 1776-1779, 2048-2051; backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:1710-1717, 1745-1761, 3016-3025; backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:677-715; backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4755-4790; backend/src/services/orderCosting.service.ts:143-252; scripts/hooks/drift-detectors.js:1212-1218
findings.detail: (a) Cloned RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION CAD row — NOT viable. order.controller.ts:677-714 copies only styleFabricId, greigeId, cutableWidth, cadMeters/Yards/Average, cadWastagePercent, markerEfficiency, purpose(+Enum), clonedFromOrderId, clonedFromCadId, notes, greigeCostPerMeter, processingPricePerMeter, totalCostPerMeter, costInputMode and sizeBreakdowns. It DROPS processorId, rateCardId, orderQuantityPcs, costingStyleId, componentName, transportCostPerMeter, shrinkagePercent/Cost, screenCost/Type, numberOfColors. With costingStyleId null the clone is invisible to every RM reader keyed on costingStyleId (style-costing-calc.controller.ts:100-108 gate and :158-172 fallback) and it trips the report-only R2 invariant (backend/scripts/check-phantom-approved-costings.ts:74-78: cost set + costingStyleId null). clonedFromOrderId is read in exactly one non-idempotency place in the whole backend (cad-embroidery.controller.ts:752), so these rows are de-facto style-scoped — the same cross-order contamination, one table down. (b) order_item_costing — dead end: it is a per-piece rollup (schema.prisma:4755-4790) with NO processorId/rateCardId/per-meter columns, written only by orderCosting.service.recalculate (:215-252), and nothing in the BOM/MRP/PO/JWO pricing chain reads it. (c) order_bom_items — BEST FIT. It is order-scoped by construction (order_bom.orderId required, `@@unique([orderId, styleId, version])`, schema.prisma:161-191); it ALREADY carries processorId, rateCardId, greigeCost, processingCost columns purpose-built for this (schema.prisma:241-246, and the comment at :243-244 designates greigeCost/processingCost as exactly what MRP prices greige POs and PROCESSING requirements at); those columns are single-writer — the only writers are order-bom.service.ts createMany paths (:1402/:1615/:1831/:2027 populated from :1106-1109, :1213-1235, :1558-1561, :1737-1740, :1776-1779, :2048-2051), while mrp.service.ts:1140/1163 touch only fabricId/laceId and order-bom.service.ts:2933 only fabricId. The value already flows end-to-end: order_bom_items.processingCost → material_requirements.processingCost/unitPrice/rateSource='ORDER_BOM'/orderBomItemId (mrp.service.ts:1710-1717, 1745-1761) → JWO agreedRatePerMeter (mrp.service.ts:3112 → 3346-3350 → 2796). Crucially it never touches fabric_width_cad, so it is subject to NO approval machinery, NO 6-column or partial unique index, and the smart-check 'CAD/costing approval drift' rule does not even scope those files (drift-detectors.js:1214-1215 SCOPED regex covers only fabric-costing*, style-costing-calc.controller, order.controller, style.service).
findings.planImpact: REPLACE the plan's 'block and force re-cost on the Fabric Costing page' with: at order confirmation, re-run processor-rate-v2 lookupRate at the ORDER quantity and write the result to that order's order_bom_items.rateCardId + processingCost (+ recompute unitPrice/totalCost for the line); at JWO creation, re-run it again at the netted quantity and write to material_requirements.processingCost/unitPrice with rateSource='RATE_CARD'. Surface the slab change as a warning/approval on the ORDER, never as an edit to the style-level fabric_width_cad row. This leaves order 1's approved basis byte-identical, needs no schema change, no index change, and no new writer on any approval column.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: repeat-order idempotency hole — the RM-clone skip check is style-scoped, so order 2 of the same style re-clones the whole RM set
findings.evidence: backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:608-628; backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4682
findings.detail: `existingRawMat` is a findFirst over ALL RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION rows whose styleFabric belongs to the style — no order filter, no ordering (order.controller.ts:608-617). The skip fires only when that arbitrarily-chosen row's clonedFromOrderId equals the CURRENT order id (:620). For House-of-Kasya-style repeat orders, order 2 finds order 1's row, the equality fails, and the clone loop runs again — producing a second full set of RM rows for the same style/component/width. Nothing at the DB level stops it: the 6-column unique index is satisfied because the clones set costingStyleId = null and componentName = null (they are simply not copied at :677-714), and NULLs are distinct in Postgres.
findings.planImpact: A repeat-buyer scenario already accumulates duplicate RM CAD rows today, independent of the rate bug. If the fix plan writes an order-adjusted rate onto the RM CAD clone, it inherits this duplication. Another point in favour of order_bom_items, whose `@@unique([orderId, styleId, version])` makes duplication structurally impossible.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: the quantity-change clone already exists and already hides the superseded parent on the Fabric Costing page — the re-cost UX the plan assumes is half-built but dead-ends
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/FabricCostingPage.tsx:1396-1404, 1432-1434; backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:1007-1073; backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:583-590; frontend/src/types/fabricCosting.types.ts:459
findings.detail: The frontend already detects `quantityChanged = savedQty != null && savedQty > 0 && currentQty !== savedQty && currentQty > 0` and switches to clone mode by sending cloneFromCadId with fabricWidthCadId null (FabricCostingPage.tsx:1397-1404); orderQuantityPcs is sent per row at :1434. The backend creates a new row with clonedFromCadId lineage and both approvals reset (fabric-costing.controller.ts:1009-1073). getStyleFabrics then EXCLUDES any row referenced as another row's clonedFromCadId — 'only the tip of each chain survives' (fabric-costing.controller.ts:583-590) — so after re-costing at order-2 quantity, order 1's approved row DISAPPEARS from the Fabric Costing page while remaining APPROVED in the DB and on the Options page (getCostingOptions at :1170+ applies no such filter). Note also this clone path is skipped entirely for approved rows (finding 1), so it can only ever fire on an already-unapproved row.
findings.planImpact: Do not build a new 're-cost at order quantity' UI on top of this: it produces a row that cannot be CAD-approved (finding 2), is invisible to the order gate (finding 3), and hides the still-authoritative parent from the very page the user is told to fix things on. If the order_bom_items route is taken, this clone path should be left alone or explicitly documented as style-level scenario modelling, not order re-costing.

findings.title: Invariants the fix must not break (check-phantom-approved-costings.ts) — and one it already violates today
findings.evidence: backend/scripts/check-phantom-approved-costings.ts:10-19, 30-46, 48-66, 68-78, 80-84; backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:677-714; backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:1615-1624
findings.detail: The sweep enforces: E1 — costingApprovalStatus set ⇒ totalCostPerMeter non-null (auto-fix clears the 3 approval fields + isPreferred, :30-46); E2 — costingApprovalStatus set ⇒ costingStyleId non-null (auto-fix backfills from styleFabric→style_components.styleId, :48-66); R1 — report-only: isLocked PRODUCTION rows with null cost (:68-72); R2 — report-only: totalCostPerMeter set with costingStyleId null (:74-78); I1 — approvalStatus APPROVED + cost null is LEGITIMATE ('CAD-approved, not yet costed', :80-84). deleteCostingOption already honours E1 belt-and-braces (fabric-costing.controller.ts:1615-1624). IMPORTANT: the order-confirmation RM clone already violates R2 today — it writes greigeCostPerMeter/processingPricePerMeter/totalCostPerMeter (order.controller.ts:697-699) but never sets costingStyleId, so every confirmed order adds R2 rows. Any fix that writes cost or approval onto a fabric_width_cad row must set costingStyleId in the same statement, and must never create an APPROVED row without a price.
findings.planImpact: If the plan insists on any fabric_width_cad write, it must (a) set costingStyleId, (b) never set a costing approval without a price, and (c) not increase R2. Storing on order_bom_items sidesteps all three constraints; separately, worth adding costingStyleId to the order.controller.ts:677-714 clone to stop the existing R2 growth.

findings.title: PREMISE CORRECTION: backend/src/services/helpers/master-config.ts contains no data-ownership rules for costing — the ownership contract lives in CLAUDE.md + CAD_OWNED_FIELDS + the drift detector
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/helpers/master-config.ts:1-31, 33-278; CLAUDE.md:120-152; backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:908-942; scripts/hooks/drift-detectors.js:1203-1241; scripts/hooks/smart-check.js:396-405

findings.title: CAD/costing approval drift check is SCOPED to order.controller.ts — any new bare `approvalStatus` line the plan adds there blocks the commit, and its baseline is empty
findings.evidence: scripts/hooks/drift-detectors.js:1212-1241 (SCOPED regex at :1214-1215 = `^backend/src/(controllers/(fabric-costing[^/]*|style-costing-calc\.controller|order\.controller)\.ts|services/style\.service\.ts)$`); scripts/hooks/smart-check.js:397-406 + :1030; scripts/hooks/costing-approval-drift-baseline.json (contents = `[]`, 3 bytes); backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:638 (existing opt-out `approvalStatus: 'APPROVED', // allow-cad-approval`); CLAUDE.md:145,165
findings.detail: The detector is case-sensitive and fires on any line in the four scoped files containing `\bapprovalStatus\b` that is not (a) a prose comment, (b) the response alias shape `approvalStatus: x.costingApproval...`, or (c) carrying `// allow-cad-approval` within the 2 preceding lines or inline. The plan's rate re-check in updateOrderStatus (order.controller.ts:563-756) will almost certainly re-query fabric_width_cad rows for the both-approvals gate — every such `approvalStatus:` filter line needs `// allow-cad-approval` (CAD half) and every price-semantics read must use `costingApprovalStatus`.
findings.planImpact: Add a compliance step: every new/edited line in order.controller.ts touching `approvalStatus` must either use `costingApprovalStatus` or carry `// allow-cad-approval` on the line or within 2 lines above. Do NOT add keys to costing-approval-drift-baseline.json (it is empty by design).

findings.title: `lookupRateWithSlab` already exists as `lookupRate` in processor-rate-v2.service.ts and already returns slabId/slabLabel/min/max — the plan would create a duplicate rate authority
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/processor-rate-v2.service.ts:877-985 (`export async function lookupRate(query: RateLookupQuery): Promise<RateLookupResult|null>`); backend/src/types/processor-rate-v2.types.ts:132-157 (RateLookupResult already carries `slabId`, `slabLabel`, `minQuantity`, `maxQuantity`, `ratePerMeter`, `totalCost`, `shrinkagePercent`, `screenCostPerScreen`); backend/src/controllers/fabric-costing.controller.ts:819 `lookupProcessorRate`; backend/src/schemas/fabricCosting.schema.ts:24-30 `lookupRateSchema`
findings.detail: lookupRate already does the half-open slab match `minQuantity <= q < maxQuantity` (drift-detectors-documented BH-0329 fix at processor-rate-v2.service.ts:904-911), falls back to the top slab, resolves SYSTEM_DEFAULT when processorId is absent, and returns full slab metadata. A new `lookupRateWithSlab` would be a second implementation of the same rule — exactly the dual-source drift the repo's own guardrails exist to prevent.
findings.planImpact: Replace 'add lookupRateWithSlab' with 'reuse/extract processor-rate-v2.service.lookupRate'. If the JWO/order paths need it, export it (it is already exported and in the `default` bag at :1738) rather than writing a parallel function.

findings.title: A SECOND, quantity-blind and greige-blind rate resolver already prices the MRP→JWO path — `resolveProcessingRate` ignores slabId and greigeId entirely
findings.evidence: backend/src/services/po-rate-resolver.service.ts:210-232 (`processor_rate_card.findFirst({ where: { processorId, isActive, ...printingType }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }, select: { ratePerMeter } })`); called from backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:52 (import), :4995-5014 (PROCESSING preview), and mirrored in generatePOFromRequirements
findings.detail: The PROCESSING branch of resolveRate picks the newest active rate card for the processor with no greigeId filter and no slab/quantity filter. findings.evidence: backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4555+ `orderQuantityPcs Int?`; frontend/src/pages/FabricCostingPage.tsx:1130-1136 (`rowQty = row.rowQuantity || orderQuantity; rowQuantityMeters = row.cadMeters * rowQty`), :1139-1176 (batchQuantityMeters aggregation over newest-per-fabric rows), :1182-1188 (lookupRate called with `hasBatchGroup ? batchQuantityMeters : rowQuantityMeters`), :1212-1222 (result stored to local state as slabLabel/rateCardId/batchGroupTotalQuantity — slabLabel and batchGroupTotalQuantity are NEVER persisted), :1419-1434 (save payload sends rateCardId and `orderQuantityPcs: row.rowQuantity ?? orderQuantity ?? 0` — pieces, not meters); backend/src/schemas/fabricCosting.schema.ts:29 `quantityMeters: z.number().positive()`; backend/src/services/processor-rate-v2.service.ts:899-911 (slab matched on quantityMeters)
findings.detail: The slab is chosen on METERS (cadMeters × pieces), and for a batch group on the SUM across sibling rows — but the DB only keeps `orderQuantityPcs` (pieces, per row). Reconstructing the costed lookup quantity from stored data is therefore impossible for batched rows. This is the concrete justification for `costedAtQuantityMeters`, but it must record the quantity ACTUALLY passed to lookupRate (batch total when processingBatchGroupColorId is set), not cadMeters × orderQuantityPcs — otherwise the order-confirmation re-check will report a spurious variance on every batched row.
findings.planImpact: Specify in the plan that costedAtQuantityMeters stores the exact lookupRate input (batch total for grouped rows) and that a companion flag/column records whether it was a batch lookup. Also persist slabLabel/min/max (currently discarded at FabricCostingPage.tsx:1214) — that is the rateSlab* columns' real job.

findings.title: swallowed-write guardrail (empty baseline) fires if a rate re-lookup try/catch wraps a Prisma write and the catch only logs

findings.detail: The plan's rate re-lookup will naturally be written as `try { rate = await lookupRate(...) } catch { /* fall back to snapshot */ }`. That is fine ONLY if no `prisma.*.create/update/...` call sits inside the same try block. If the re-lookup and the JWO/CAD write share a try, and the catch only logs, it is a fresh violation against an empty baseline.
findings.planImpact: Instruct: keep the rate lookup in its own try/catch, separate from any Prisma write; if a write must be inside, the catch must rethrow/respond/set a surfaced flag or carry `// allow-swallow`.

additionalFromCritic.title: Costing-time CAD approval permanently reserves fabric stock at the COSTED quantity, and nothing ever releases it — MRP nets the JWO quantity against a phantom reservation
additionalFromCritic.evidence: backend/src/controllers/cad-approval.controller.ts:19-85 (reserveFabricStock), :27 (quantityNeeded = cadAverage × orderQuantityPcs), :64-71 (raw quantityReserved += ), :171-185 (called on PRODUCTION CAD approval); backend/src/services/mrp.service.ts:1310-1328 (netFreeStock subtracts quantityReserved); repo-wide grep 'quantityReserved' — cad-approval.controller.ts:69 is the ONLY incrementer of fabric_stock.quantityReserved; the only decrementers are greige_stock (backend/src/services/job-work-issuance.service.ts:517-527) and lace_stock (backend/src/services/laceIssueNote.service.ts:210,:317)
additionalFromCritic.detail: Approving a PRODUCTION CAD row with a fabricStockId bumps fabric_stock.quantityReserved by cadAverage × fabric_width_cad.orderQuantityPcs — the manually typed COSTING quantity. The write is a bare += with no orderId, no stock_reservations ledger row (contrast job-work-issuance.service.ts:511-514 which releases via stock_reservations), and no counterpart in rejectCADPurpose or anywhere else. MRP's fabric branch computes free stock as quantityAvailable − quantityReserved, so a costing-time 2500-pc reservation permanently shrinks the stock the real 700-pc order can net against — which in turn inflates the shortfall and therefore the JWO quantity that any new slab re-lookup would use.
additionalFromCritic.planImpact: A rate re-lookup keyed on 'the quantity the JWO will actually dispatch' inherits this corruption. The plan must either exclude CAD-approval reservations from netting or add a release path; otherwise the re-looked-up slab is computed from a quantity that is itself wrong.

additionalFromCritic.title: Lace has a SECOND slab-aware resolver (lookupLaceRate) called only at costing, and the order quantity there also decides the SOURCING STRATEGY — neither is ever re-evaluated
additionalFromCritic.evidence: backend/src/services/processor-rate-v2.service.ts:1608-1700 (lookupLaceRate: same half-open slab match at :1629-1634, top-slab fallback :1639-1648, SYSTEM_DEFAULT processor fallback :1612-1621); backend/src/services/laceCostingCalculation.service.ts:123 (orderQuantity = 1 default), :177 (totalQuantityNeeded = effectiveQuantity × orderQuantity), :180-191 (three strategies costed at that quantity), :285-290 (stock strategy requires a SINGLE lot with quantityAvailable >= quantityNeeded), :578-582 and :616-620 (lookupLaceRate calls), :233-256 (cheapest strategy wins); backend/prisma/schema.prisma:2070-2125 (style_costing_lace_items: sourcingStrategy, costPerMeter, rateCardId — and NO quantity column); backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:1260-1297 (BOM line: unitPrice = laceItem.costPerMeter, totalQuantity = qtyPerGarment × the REAL orderQuantity, sourcingStrategy copied verbatim); frontend/src/components/cost-sheet/LaceCostingSection.tsx:20,:244 and LaceCostingRow.tsx:18,:85 (orderQuantity threaded from styles.orderQuantity, schema.prisma:207 — a THIRD quantity source distinct from fabric_width_cad.orderQuantityPcs and order_items.totalQuantity)
additionalFromCritic.detail: Lace repeats the whole fabric defect in a parallel code path the audit never opened, and adds a worse one: the quantity does not merely pick a rate slab, it picks the SOURCING STRATEGY (Stock Reuse vs Ready Lace vs Greige+Dyeing) via a single-lot availability test. Drop the order from 2500 to 700 and stock reuse may now be feasible and cheapest; raise it and the single-lot test fails. The decision and its costPerMeter are frozen in style_costing_lace_items, which has no quantity column at all, then re-multiplied by the real order quantity in the BOM. Note also lookupLaceRate hard-codes processingType 'DYEING' and defaults orderQuantity to 1 when the caller omits it — the lowest slab.
additionalFromCritic.planImpact: The plan is fabric-only. Lace needs its own re-check, and it is not just a rate re-check — it is a strategy re-check. lookupLaceRate returns slab.id (not slabId) and no rateCard.id, so provenance capture differs from lookupRate.

additionalFromCritic.planImpact: Any post-issue rate change the plan introduces (a slab correction at receipt, a variance acknowledgement) must call computeCommercialTotals AND decide which of agreedRate/actualRate is the tax base — today the two silently disagree.

additionalFromCritic.title: MOQ is modelled on four masters and read by nothing — a shrunken order silently produces sub-MOQ purchase orders and JWOs
additionalFromCritic.evidence: backend/prisma/schema.prisma:142-143 (material_supplier_mapping.moq/moqUnit), :2957-2958 (a second supplier-mapping model's moq/moqUnit), :4292 (greige_master.moq), :4496 (fabric_master.moq), :4865 (fabric_procurement.processingMoq, whose docstring at :4844 says 'for MOQ excess tracking'); repo-wide case-insensitive grep for 'moq' across backend/src returns only CRUD/type/schema/enum hits (fabric.controller, greige.controller, material.controller/service, trimMasters.schema, fabricStock EXCESS_MOQ enum) — zero hits in mrp.service.ts, po-rate-resolver.service.ts, order-bom.service.ts, dyeing.controller.ts, printing.controller.ts or job-work-order.controller.ts

additionalFromCritic.title: Order creation silently replaces the typed total quantity with the size-breakup sum, while the UI treats the mismatch as informational and prices the order off the typed total
additionalFromCritic.evidence: backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:173-174 (`const itemTotalQty = breakupQty > 0 ? breakupQty : item.totalQuantity || 0`), :177 (totalPrice computed from itemTotalQty), :808 (same rule in updateOrder); frontend/src/pages/OrderForm.tsx:898-904 (quantityMismatch — comment says 'informational, not blocking'), :919-935 (validation has no distribution check; comment 'size distribution is now OPTIONAL'), :892-896 (totalAmount displayed = enteredTotalQty × unitPrice), :994 and :1006-1007 (payload sends BOTH totalQuantity and breakup)

additionalFromCritic.title: PARTIAL/REFUTES the 'PUT /orders/:id freely replaces items' finding: the guard also blocks on ANY non-cancelled requirement, the UI disables the quantity input, and body.totalQuantity is silently ignored
additionalFromCritic.evidence: backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:782-797 (guard counts approved/locked BOMs AND material_requirements with status notIn ['CANCELLED']), :768-775 (updateData is built without totalQuantity — the body field is never read), :800 (recompute and item replacement only run when items is a non-empty array); frontend/src/pages/OrderForm.tsx:439-444 (hasDownstreamDeps = approved/locked BOM OR any materialRequirements row), :1146-1154 (quantity Input `disabled={hasDownstreamDeps}`), :1000-1010 (items omitted entirely when hasDownstreamDeps), :994 (totalQuantity still sent and silently dropped), :1067-1074 (warning text: 'Style, quantity, and size breakdown cannot be changed. Either the plan must define a supported short-close path, or the re-check has to live entirely on the JWO side because the order quantity can no longer move by then.

additionalFromCritic.title: Thread BOM lines scale 1:1 with garment pieces in a fabricated 'LOT' unit that MRP does not recognise and silently downgrades to PIECE

additionalFromCritic.detail: A per-garment thread COST is modelled as a per-garment QUANTITY. For a 1500-piece order MRP raises a requirement for 1500 'LOT' of thread, normalised to 1500 PIECE, and a purchase order is generated against that. The rupee total happens to be right; the procurement quantity is nonsense and scales linearly with the order quantity — which is exactly the axis the plan is auditing.
additionalFromCritic.planImpact: A non-fabric material whose requirement quantity is quantity-derived and unit-broken. Any quantity-consistency check the plan adds across cost sheet → BOM → requirement will flag or mis-flag thread unless LOT is handled.

additionalFromCritic.title: getMasterRecordPrice covers only 7 legacy trim masters — the 16 generic trim masters have no price fallback and land at unitPrice 0
additionalFromCritic.evidence: backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:2685-2702 (button/thread/zipper/elastic/label/packaging/lace only), :685-706 (price chain: cost-sheet trimRate → accessoryRate → material.unitPrice → getMasterRecordPrice → warn and leave 0), :722-737 (all 16 generic trim FKs ARE populated on the BOM line: hookEyeId, snapButtonId, buckleId, beltId, velcroId, drawstringId, ribbonId, sequinId, beadId, motifId, interliningId, paddingId, otherFastenerId, otherTapeId, otherDecorativeId, otherFunctionalId)
additionalFromCritic.detail: The BOM knows which buckle/ribbon/interlining master a line points at but has no branch to read its price, so unless the cost sheet carried an explicit trimRate the line is created at ₹0 with only a log warning. The material cost of the order is understated by exactly those lines, and MRP then buys them with unitPrice null → the po-rate-resolver TRIMS chain (po-rate-resolver.service.ts:234-297: supplier price → legacy bridge → material_master.pricePerUnit) which has no quantity tiers either.
additionalFromCritic.planImpact: Non-fabric materials have no quantity-based pricing anywhere in this system — supplierPrice is a single flat scalar (schema.prisma:140). The plan's 'trims with qty-based pricing' concern is moot for trims but the ₹0 hole is real and will corrupt any BOM-vs-cost-sheet reconciliation the plan adds.

additionalFromCritic.title: cadAverage assumes the marker's size ratio equals the order's size mix — order_item_breakup is never read by CAD, costing or BOM
additionalFromCritic.evidence: backend/src/controllers/cad-planning.controller.ts:1610-1615 (piecesPerMarker = Σ cad_size_breakdown.quantity), backend/src/controllers/cad-planning.utils.ts:123-134 (calculateCadAverage = (cadMeters + layerMargin) ÷ piecesPerMarker); backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4737-4745 (cad_size_breakdown.quantity); backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:702-713 (the order-confirmation RM clone copies the COSTED sizeBreakdowns verbatim); grep for order_item_breakup in cad-planning.controller.ts, fabric-costing.controller.ts and order-bom.service.ts returns zero matches
additionalFromCritic.detail: Meters per piece is derived from a marker whose size composition is stored on the CAD row. The order's actual per-size quantities live in order_item_breakup and are never consulted by CAD planning, fabric costing or BOM generation. A 700-piece re-cut skewed to XL consumes more per piece than the marker implies, so BOM meters (= cadAverage × orderQuantity) are wrong independently of the rate. The RM clone at order confirmation propagates the costed size ratio rather than the order's.
additionalFromCritic.planImpact: 'Re-cost at the order quantity' is incomplete if the size mix also changed. If the plan stores a costedAtQuantityMeters, note that meters is a function of both the piece count and the size mix, and only the piece count is currently in scope.

additionalFromCritic.title: Samples are outside the entire quantity/rate machinery, and the generic JWO endpoint creates order-less, style-optional jobs with a hand-typed rate
additionalFromCritic.evidence: backend/prisma/schema.prisma:1627-1666 (samples model: no quantity, no BOM, no requirement, no job_work_order relation), :4794-4814 (order_samples: sampleType only), :9476-9483 (SampleType enum); backend/src/controllers/job-work-order.controller.ts:203 (jobWorkNumber uses `style?.styleCode || 'STK'`), :211 (styleId: body.styleId ?? null), :205-243 (no orderId field exists on the create at all), :232 (agreedRatePerMeter: isKaaj ? 0 : body.agreedRate), :196-201 (expectedShrinkage taken from the body for stock jobs); backend/src/services/work-order-service-requirement.service.ts:1108 (same 'STK' fallback)
additionalFromCritic.detail: There is no sample order, no sample BOM and no sample quantity anywhere in the schema. Sample yardage is processed through the generic 'stock' JWO path: no order, optional style, no material requirement, no cost sheet, an operator-typed rate and an operator-typed expected shrinkage. Sample meters are typically tiny, so any slab lookup would land in the lowest-quantity (highest-rate) tier — which is commercially correct for samples but would be indistinguishable from a production-order regression if the plan starts comparing looked-up rates against costed rates globally.
additionalFromCritic.planImpact: The re-check must be scoped to order-linked JWOs, or every sample/stock job will raise a rate-variance alert against a cost sheet it was never derived from.

additionalFromCritic.title: style_costing.lockedForOrders is written in exactly one place and read by no backend code — the version lock is decorative
additionalFromCritic.evidence: backend/src/controllers/style-costing-approval.controller.ts:295 (`lockedForOrders: true` on the superseded version — the only writer); repo-wide grep across *.ts/*.tsx finds no backend reader: frontend/src/types/costSheet.types.ts:174, components/cost-sheet/VersionManagement.tsx:17,101,136,205,296, CostSheetComparisonModal.tsx:152, pages/CostSheetList.tsx:356, CostSheetDetail.tsx:239 — all display-only; backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:119-139 (the order gate filters on purpose, supersededById: null and isApproved, never lockedForOrders)
additionalFromCritic.detail: The schema field (schema.prisma:1881) and the version machinery (version/versionDate/versionReason/supersededById at :1882-1885) suggest an enforced lock on costings already consumed by orders. No backend gate reads it. It only renders a badge.
additionalFromCritic.planImpact: If the plan intends to 'lock the costed rate once an order consumes it', the existing flag is not a foundation — it is an unenforced label that must either be wired up or ignored to avoid implying a guarantee that does not exist.
